# GOV.UK Design System

> Category: Government & Public Services
> Clear, accessible public services built from reviewed GOV.UK guidance.

<!-- Generated by govuk-design-md. Edit src/catalog records, then run npm run generate. -->

## 1. Visual Theme & Atmosphere

This standalone OpenDesign import is generated from govuk-design-md@0.4.0, reviewed against GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09. It includes 13 foundations, 37 components and 30 patterns. Guidance and examples are embedded; no repository-relative files are required.

Start from the official GOV.UK components and preserve their semantic HTML, classes, keyboard behaviour, focus states and progressive enhancement. Visual similarity and token mappings alone do not establish GOV.UK conformance. Use the linked official guidance to check for changes after the review date.

This is a community project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the UK Government, the Government Digital Service, or the GOV.UK Design System team.

Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0: <https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/>

GOV.UK Frontend code and sample code are made available by their authors under the MIT License. See <https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend>.

GOV.UK, the GOV.UK crown, and GDS Transport are identity assets with usage requirements. This package does not redistribute them. Consumers must follow the official GOV.UK guidance for their service context.

## 2. Color Palette & Roles

### Colour

**Foundation group:** visual elements  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use GOV.UK functional colours and the refreshed palette to keep meaning, interaction states and contrast consistent across services.

#### Rules

- Always start from the current GOV.UK palette and use functional colours for essential page elements.
- In Sass use govuk-functional-colour with a purpose such as brand, text, link, focus, error or success instead of copying a hexadecimal value.
- In plain CSS use the corresponding functional custom-property alias from tokens/govuk.css; palette variables are for reviewed mappings, not new semantics.
- Preserve the full hover, visited, active, error, success and focus state system when adapting components.
- Update the pinned token set when GOV.UK Frontend changes instead of retaining an obsolete colour for visual compatibility.

#### Accessibility contract

- Text and interactive elements must meet WCAG 2.2 level AA contrast requirements in every state.
- Never use colour as the only way to communicate status, validation, selection or action hierarchy.
- Test custom colour combinations rather than assuming that two palette colours have sufficient contrast.
- Retain the yellow focus background and dark focus text unless official component guidance specifies another tested treatment.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not assign a new meaning to an existing GOV.UK functional colour.
- Do not claim an interface is GOV.UK-conformant because its brand blue and green values match the palette.
- This portable token export does not replace GOV.UK Frontend component CSS.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.brand`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.secondary-text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.link-visited`
- `govuk.color.link-hover`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.success`

#### Examples

##### Functional colour in plain CSS

```css
.app-status--error {
  color: var(--govuk-error-colour);
  border-left: var(--govuk-border-width) solid currentcolor;
}
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/colour/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/settings/_colours-functional.scss)

## 3. Typography

### Font override classes

**Foundation group:** typography  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use GOV.UK font override classes sparingly when content needs an explicit alignment, size, weight, number style or overflow treatment.

#### Rules

- Prefer the default typography of the component or content element before applying an override.
- Use govuk-!-text-align-left, -right or -centre only when the content convention requires it.
- Use reviewed govuk-!-font-size-* and govuk-!-font-weight-* classes instead of custom declarations.
- Use tabular number and break-word overrides only for content that demonstrates the need.

#### Accessibility contract

- Visual alignment and weight do not change semantic reading order or importance.
- Do not shrink essential information below standard body size.
- When breaking long words or identifiers, confirm the full value remains available and understandable to assistive technology.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not stack several override classes to redesign a component.
- Do not use typography overrides as a substitute for the correct heading, paragraph or component class.

#### Token references

- `govuk.typography.weight.regular`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`
- `govuk.typography.scale.16.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.19.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.24.mobile-font-size`

#### Examples

##### Tabular numeric data

```html
<span class="govuk-!-font-tabular-numbers">12,345.67</span>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/font-override-classes/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/overrides/_typography.scss)

### Headings

**Foundation group:** typography  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use semantic heading elements and GOV.UK heading classes to create a consistent, navigable content hierarchy.

#### Rules

- Use h1 through h6 elements for document structure and apply govuk-heading-xl, -l, -m or -s for visual size.
- Ordinarily use one clear h1, then descend through heading levels without choosing elements for their appearance.
- For common question pages, pair h1 with govuk-heading-l, h2 with govuk-heading-m and lower headings with the next suitable size.
- Use heading captions to provide context above a heading without replacing the heading itself.

#### Accessibility contract

- A heading level must reflect nesting in the page outline even when its GOV.UK size class differs.
- Do not use bold paragraphs as visual headings because screen-reader heading navigation will miss them.
- Any deliberate visual and semantic hierarchy mismatch needs accessibility testing in its full context.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not select a heading element solely to obtain its default browser size or margin.
- Avoid very long headings; simplify the content and keep the page purpose clear.

#### Token references

- `govuk.typography.scale.48.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.36.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.24.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.19.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`

#### Examples

##### Semantic page hierarchy

```html
<h1 class="govuk-heading-l">Apply for a licence</h1>
<h2 class="govuk-heading-m">Before you start</h2>
<h3 class="govuk-heading-s">What you need</h3>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/headings/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/core/_typography.scss)

### Links

**Foundation group:** typography  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use descriptive, underlined GOV.UK links for navigation and preserve their visited, hover, active and focus states.

#### Rules

- Links are blue and underlined by default; linked text at the end of a sentence must not include the full stop.
- Write link text that describes the destination or result when read out of context.
- Use govuk-link--no-visited-state only where visited history is not useful, such as frequently changing application navigation.
- Use the official inverse or no-underline variants only in their documented contexts.
- If a link opens a new tab, warn users in the link text and avoid doing so unless necessary.

#### Accessibility contract

- Retain the visible underline and GOV.UK focus treatment; colour alone must not identify a link.
- Avoid repeated vague labels such as click here or read more.
- Keep the anchor href so links work with keyboards, assistive technology and without JavaScript.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not style ordinary navigation links as buttons.
- Do not remove visited styling globally merely for visual uniformity.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.link-visited`
- `govuk.color.link-hover`
- `govuk.color.link-active`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`

#### Examples

##### Link in body content

```html
<p class="govuk-body">Read the <a class="govuk-link" href="/eligibility">eligibility guidance</a>.</p>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/links/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/core/_links.scss)

### Lists

**Foundation group:** typography  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use semantic GOV.UK lists to break information into manageable chunks and communicate whether order matters.

#### Rules

- Use ul when order does not matter and ol when sequence, rank or count matters.
- Apply govuk-list and add govuk-list--bullet or govuk-list--number for visible markers.
- Introduce a bulleted list with a lead-in line ending in a colon; normally start each item in lowercase without a final full stop.
- Use govuk-list--spaced only when longer items need extra separation.

#### Accessibility contract

- Keep native ul, ol and li elements so assistive technology announces list structure and item count.
- Do not simulate list markers with text characters or CSS on unrelated elements.
- Nested lists must reflect the actual content hierarchy.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not use a list merely to align controls or create columns.
- Avoid long, deeply nested lists; split or restructure the content when scanning becomes difficult.

#### Token references

- `govuk.typography.scale.19.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.spacing.static.1`
- `govuk.spacing.static.3`

#### Examples

##### Bulleted list

```html
<p class="govuk-body">You will need:</p>
<ul class="govuk-list govuk-list--bullet">
  <li>your licence number</li>
  <li>a payment card</li>
</ul>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/lists/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/core/_lists.scss)

### Paragraphs

**Foundation group:** typography  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use GOV.UK body classes for readable text, with lead and small variants only when their hierarchy has a clear purpose.

#### Rules

- Use govuk-body for the majority of paragraph text; its default desktop size is 19px.
- Use govuk-body-l once at most near the start of a page when an introductory summary helps users.
- Use govuk-body-s sparingly for genuinely secondary content, not to make crowded content fit.
- Keep paragraphs concise and group related sentences under descriptive headings.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use p elements for paragraphs so content retains structure without CSS.
- Do not convey importance only by size; use clear wording and semantic structure.
- Maintain readable line lengths and test body text at enlarged sizes.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not use the lead class for multiple paragraphs on the same page.
- Do not make the majority of service content small body text.

#### Token references

- `govuk.typography.scale.24.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.19.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.16.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.color.text`

#### Examples

##### Lead and standard body copy

```html
<p class="govuk-body-l">Use this service to renew your licence.</p>
<p class="govuk-body">You will need your current licence number.</p>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/paragraphs/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/core/_typography.scss)

### Type scale

**Foundation group:** typography  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the responsive GOV.UK type scale so text sizes and line heights retain the tested rhythm introduced in GOV.UK Frontend 6.

#### Rules

- Start with existing GOV.UK typography classes or the govuk-font mixin before creating any custom text style.
- If a custom component needs a size, align it to one of the reviewed 80, 48, 36, 27, 24, 19 or 16 scale points.
- Use the corresponding reviewed line height; scale points use multiples of 5px to preserve vertical rhythm.
- Use responsive values above the tablet breakpoint and allow GOV.UK Frontend to output relative CSS units.

#### Accessibility contract

- Do not set a root font size that prevents user font-size preferences from taking effect.
- Prefer rem or em in rendered CSS so browser zoom and text magnification behave predictably.
- Test every custom combination at 200% and 400% zoom and with long translated content.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not add intermediate font sizes merely to make a layout fit; change the layout or select the nearest tested scale point.
- Do not use the 80 or 27 points for ordinary headings; the official guidance reserves them for exceptional cases.

#### Token references

- `govuk.typography.scale.16.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.19.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.24.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.27.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.36.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.48.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.typography.scale.80.mobile-font-size`
- `govuk.breakpoint.tablet`

#### Examples

##### Apply a reviewed type-scale point in Sass

```scss
.app-summary {
  @include govuk-font($size: 24);
}
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/type-scale/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/settings/_typography-responsive.scss)

### Typeface

**Foundation group:** typography  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the approved GOV.UK typeface only for eligible services and configure an appropriate alternative for services outside the GOV.UK proposition.

#### Rules

- A service on the service.gov.uk subdomain must use GDS Transport through the official GOV.UK Frontend asset setup.
- A publicly available service on another subdomain must configure an alternative typeface using the official unbranded GOV.UK Frontend guidance.
- Use regular weight 400 for body text and bold weight 700 for emphasis and headings unless a component specifies otherwise.
- Use system fonts for print output as configured by GOV.UK Frontend.

#### Accessibility contract

- Do not prevent users from resizing text or substituting fonts through browser and assistive-technology settings.
- Test fallback fonts for reflow, clipping and control sizing because their metrics differ from GDS Transport.
- Use semantic emphasis and heading elements rather than font weight alone to communicate structure.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- GDS Transport is restricted to services on the GOV.UK domain; this package names the typeface for guidance but does not distribute, embed or license the font files.
- Do not copy font files from GOV.UK pages or from another service.

#### Token references

- `govuk.typography.weight.regular`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`

#### Examples

##### Unbranded font configuration

```scss
@use "govuk-frontend/dist/govuk" as govuk with (
  $govuk-font-family: (arial, sans-serif),
  $govuk-include-default-font-face: false
);
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/typeface/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/settings/_typography-font.scss)

## 4. Layout & Spacing

### Layout

**Foundation group:** page structure  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use GOV.UK wrappers and grid classes to create mobile-first pages with readable line lengths and predictable responsive behaviour.

#### Rules

- Design small screens first as a single column, then introduce columns at reviewed GOV.UK breakpoints.
- Wrap page content with govuk-width-container and govuk-main-wrapper before using the grid.
- For most pages use a two-thirds content column, or a two-thirds and one-third layout, to keep text to roughly 75 characters per line.
- Use the GOV.UK grid classes and width overrides instead of inventing near-equivalent breakpoints or column percentages.
- The standard width container is 960px of content plus gutters, producing a default maximum outer width of 1020px.

#### Accessibility contract

- Keep DOM reading order meaningful when columns collapse or CSS is unavailable.
- Do not use visual reordering to create a different keyboard or screen-reader sequence.
- Use govuk-visually-hidden only for content that must remain available to assistive technology; do not use display:none for that purpose.
- Test zoom, text resizing and narrow layouts without horizontal scrolling for ordinary content.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not select a breakpoint because it matches a named device; respond to available space and content needs.
- Only widen the default container when the content has a demonstrated need, such as a data-heavy interface.

#### Token references

- `govuk.breakpoint.mobile`
- `govuk.breakpoint.tablet`
- `govuk.breakpoint.desktop`
- `govuk.layout.page-width`
- `govuk.layout.gutter`
- `govuk.layout.gutter-half`

#### Examples

##### Two-thirds content column

```html
<div class="govuk-width-container">
  <main class="govuk-main-wrapper" id="main-content">
    <div class="govuk-grid-row">
      <div class="govuk-grid-column-two-thirds">
        <h1 class="govuk-heading-xl">Page title</h1>
      </div>
    </div>
  </main>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/layout/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/objects)

### Page template

**Foundation group:** page structure  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the GOV.UK page template to supply the document structure, assets and shared components required for a consistent GOV.UK page.

#### Rules

- Prefer the Nunjucks page template supplied by GOV.UK Frontend so template changes arrive with dependency updates.
- When translating the template to another framework, preserve the document language, UTF-8 declaration, viewport-fit setting, theme colour, body classes, asset links, skip link, header, main landmark, footer and JavaScript initialisation.
- Run the official body-start support snippet before rendering enhanced components; it adds js-enabled and govuk-frontend-supported only in capable browsers.
- Place the main page content in a uniquely identified main element targeted by the skip link.

#### Accessibility contract

- Set the html lang attribute to the language of the page and use pageTitleLang or equivalent when the title differs.
- Keep the skip link as the first useful focusable control and make its target ID resolve to the main landmark.
- Set a unique, descriptive page title and retain browser zoom by using the official viewport declaration.
- Do not hide unenhanced component content while waiting for JavaScript.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- The default GOV.UK header, footer, crown, favicon and other identity assets are only for eligible services; non-GOV.UK services must follow the official unbranded configuration guidance.
- Plain HTML copies do not receive upstream template fixes automatically and must be reviewed whenever GOV.UK Frontend changes.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.brand`
- `govuk.color.body-background`
- `govuk.color.template-background`
- `govuk.layout.page-width`

#### Examples

##### Essential document shell

```html
<!doctype html>
<html class="govuk-template" lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover">
    <title>Service page</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/govuk-frontend.min.css">
  </head>
  <body class="govuk-template__body">
    <script>document.body.className += ' js-enabled' + ('noModule' in HTMLScriptElement.prototype ? ' govuk-frontend-supported' : '');</script>
    <a class="govuk-skip-link" href="#main-content" data-module="govuk-skip-link">Skip to main content</a>
    <main class="govuk-main-wrapper" id="main-content"></main>
  </body>
</html>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/page-template/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/template.njk)

### Section break

**Foundation group:** page structure  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a GOV.UK section break on an hr element to create a thematic break with standard spacing and an optional visible rule.

#### Rules

- Use an hr element with govuk-section-break when the content has a genuine thematic break.
- Select govuk-section-break--m, --l or --xl for the required standard margin.
- Add govuk-section-break--visible only when users need a visible separator; the default break is represented by spacing alone.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use the native hr semantic only for a thematic change, not as decoration.
- Do not rely on the separator line as the only cue that a new subject or task begins.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not use empty div elements, repeated hyphens or CSS borders as substitutes for the documented section-break contract.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.spacing.static.3`
- `govuk.spacing.static.6`
- `govuk.spacing.static.9`

#### Examples

##### Large visible section break

```html
<hr class="govuk-section-break govuk-section-break--l govuk-section-break--visible">
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/section-break/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/blob/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/core/_section-break.scss)

### Spacing

**Foundation group:** page structure  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the GOV.UK static and responsive spacing scales to maintain a consistent vertical rhythm and predictable component separation.

#### Rules

- Use responsive spacing for page and component layout unless a measurement must remain fixed across breakpoints.
- Spacing units 0 to 3 stay fixed; responsive units 4 to 9 increase at the tablet breakpoint.
- In Sass, prefer govuk-responsive-margin, govuk-responsive-padding and govuk-spacing helpers.
- In HTML, use GOV.UK spacing override classes sparingly and only when a component's default spacing does not fit the content relationship.
- Keep additions on the 5px-based scale rather than inventing arbitrary near-values.

#### Accessibility contract

- Spacing must survive text resizing and content expansion without clipping or overlap.
- Do not use whitespace instead of semantic grouping or headings.
- Do not tighten interactive controls below their usable pointer and touch target area.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Avoid chains of override classes that obscure the component's intended layout.
- Do not use negative spacing points unless the official helper explicitly supports the property and the result has been tested.

## 5. Components

### Accordion

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use an accordion to let users reveal and hide related sections when showing all of the content at once would make a page difficult to scan.

#### When to use

- Use for several related sections when users need only some of the content and can understand each section from its heading.
- Consider simplifying or splitting the page before introducing an accordion.
- Use expanded sections sparingly when a section is likely to be needed immediately.

#### When not to use

- Do not hide information that most users need to complete the current task.
- Do not use an accordion as a substitute for a clear page structure or a sequence of service steps.
- Do not use it for content that users need to compare across sections at the same time.

#### Anatomy

- **Accordion container (required):** A uniquely identified container carries govuk-accordion and data-module="govuk-accordion".
- **Section (required):** Each repeated section contains one header and one content region.
- **Section heading (required):** A heading at the correct document level contains the section-button hook and a unique ID.
- **Section content (required):** The content region has a unique ID associated with the same accordion and section position.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-accordion` | Related sections start collapsed after enhancement while remaining visible without JavaScript. |
| Expanded section | `div` | `govuk-accordion__section`, `govuk-accordion__section--expanded` | A section whose content should be open when the enhanced component first appears. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise the official govuk-accordion module from GOV.UK Frontend.
- Without JavaScript, all section content remains visible under ordinary headings.
- With JavaScript, GOV.UK Frontend creates disclosure controls, state text, and show-all behaviour.
- Container, heading, and content IDs must be unique on the page.

#### Accessibility contract

- Choose heading elements that preserve the page's logical heading hierarchy.
- Section headings must identify the content clearly when read independently.
- Do not hand-build the enhanced button and ARIA state; initialise the official module from the documented base markup.
- Do not hide the unenhanced content before GOV.UK Frontend confirms JavaScript support.

#### Content rules

- Use short, descriptive section headings.
- Place the information users need to decide whether to expand a section in its heading or optional summary.
- Avoid repeating the same opening words across every heading when distinctive wording is available.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.text`

#### HTML examples

##### Two-section accordion

```html
<div class="govuk-accordion" data-module="govuk-accordion" id="accordion-guidance">
  <div class="govuk-accordion__section">
    <div class="govuk-accordion__section-header">
      <h2 class="govuk-accordion__section-heading">
        <span class="govuk-accordion__section-button" id="accordion-guidance-heading-1">
          Writing well for the web
        </span>
      </h2>
    </div>
    <div id="accordion-guidance-content-1" class="govuk-accordion__section-content">
      <p class="govuk-body">This is the content for Writing well for the web.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="govuk-accordion__section">
    <div class="govuk-accordion__section-header">
      <h2 class="govuk-accordion__section-heading">
        <span class="govuk-accordion__section-button" id="accordion-guidance-heading-2">
          Know your audience
        </span>
      </h2>
    </div>
    <div id="accordion-guidance-content-2" class="govuk-accordion__section-content">
      <p class="govuk-body">This is the content for Know your audience.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Back link

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a back link to return users to the previous page, in its previous state, within a multi-page transaction.

#### When to use

- Always include a back link on question pages in a GOV.UK service.
- Use it on another page in a multi-page transaction when returning to the previous state helps users.

#### When not to use

- Never use a back link and breadcrumbs together on the same page.
- Do not use it as a general navigation link to an unrelated or fixed destination.

#### Anatomy

- **Anchor (required):** A real href returns to the previous page and retains its state without requiring JavaScript.
- **Label (required):** Usually “Back”; a complex journey may name the destination to remove ambiguity.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `a` | `govuk-back-link` | At the top of an ordinary service page. |
| Inverse | `a` | `govuk-back-link`, `govuk-back-link--inverse` | On a dark background that maintains at least 4.5:1 contrast with white. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Place the link before the main element so the page skip link can bypass it with other navigation.
- Prefer a server-generated href. If it cannot work without JavaScript, hide it until JavaScript is available.
- Return the user to the prior page as they last saw it, including entered state.

#### Accessibility contract

- Keep native anchor semantics and a visible focus indicator.
- Do not move the link into main solely to silence automated landmark warnings; official guidance places it before main.
- For the inverse variant, verify white link contrast against the actual background.

#### Content rules

- Use “Back” for a simple linear journey.
- For a complex journey use specific text such as “Go back to applications” when “Back” is unclear.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`

#### HTML examples

##### Default back link

```html
<a href="/previous-step" class="govuk-back-link">Back</a>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/back-link/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/back-link)

### Breadcrumbs

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use breadcrumbs to help users understand and move between levels in a website with a deep hierarchy.

#### When to use

- Use when a site has multiple hierarchical levels and users need to understand or traverse that structure.
- Use the collapse-on-mobile variant for a long path after confirming that the first and final visible items remain useful.

#### When not to use

- Do not use on a site with a flat information architecture.
- Do not use breadcrumbs to show progress through a linear transaction.
- Never show breadcrumbs together with a back link.

#### Anatomy

- **Navigation landmark (required):** A nav element has a concise aria-label that identifies the breadcrumb navigation.
- **Ordered path (required):** An ordered list represents the hierarchy from the home page to the current page's parent.
- **Breadcrumb links (required):** Each item links to its corresponding ancestor level.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `nav` | `govuk-breadcrumbs` | A short hierarchy on the standard page background. |
| Collapse on mobile | `nav` | `govuk-breadcrumbs`, `govuk-breadcrumbs--collapse-on-mobile` | A long path that should show only its first and last items on smaller screens. |
| Inverse | `nav` | `govuk-breadcrumbs`, `govuk-breadcrumbs--inverse` | A dark background with verified contrast. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Place breadcrumbs before main so the page skip link bypasses them.
- Start at the site's home page and end at the parent of the current page; do not include the current page as a redundant final link.
- The component requires no JavaScript and every link must have a usable href.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use a nav landmark with aria-label="Breadcrumb" or an equivalent localised label.
- Retain the ordered-list structure and meaningful link text.
- Verify inverse links and separators meet contrast requirements.

#### Content rules

- Use the page or section name for each item and keep it concise.
- Ensure adjacent items are distinguishable when announced as a list of links.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`
- `govuk.breakpoint.tablet`

#### HTML examples

##### Three-level breadcrumbs

```html
<nav class="govuk-breadcrumbs" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol class="govuk-breadcrumbs__list">
    <li class="govuk-breadcrumbs__list-item"><a class="govuk-breadcrumbs__link" href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li class="govuk-breadcrumbs__list-item"><a class="govuk-breadcrumbs__link" href="/benefits">Benefits</a></li>
    <li class="govuk-breadcrumbs__list-item"><a class="govuk-breadcrumbs__link" href="/benefits/families">Families</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/breadcrumbs/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/breadcrumbs)

### Button

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a button to let a user perform a clear action, such as saving information or continuing to the next step.

#### When to use

- Use the default button for the primary action on a page or form.
- Use a start button for the entry point to a transactional service.
- Use secondary or warning variants only when the action hierarchy or destructive consequence requires them.

#### When not to use

- Do not use a button for ordinary navigation; use a link unless the link is the explicit start of a service.
- Do not place several visually primary buttons together when one action is the clear next step.
- Do not use the warning variant for a reversible or low-risk action.

#### Anatomy

- **Native action element (required):** Use a button element for actions and form submission. A start-page link may use button styling with link semantics made explicit.
- **Action label (required):** Short sentence-case text describes the action and its effect.
- **GOV.UK module hook (required):** The data-module attribute allows GOV.UK Frontend to attach its supported behaviour.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `button` | `govuk-button` | The page's main action, for example “Save and continue”. |
| Secondary | `button` | `govuk-button`, `govuk-button--secondary` | A less prominent action, for example “Find address” or “Save as draft”. |
| Warning | `button` | `govuk-button`, `govuk-button--warning` | A destructive action with serious consequences, for example “Delete account”. |
| Start | `a` | `govuk-button`, `govuk-button--start` | The single entry point to a service, labelled “Start now”. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise GOV.UK Frontend JavaScript when using data-module="govuk-button".
- Form buttons should declare an appropriate type; use type="submit" for submission and type="button" for client-side actions.
- The interface must remain understandable if JavaScript does not run.

#### Accessibility contract

- Prefer the native button element for actions so keyboard and assistive-technology behaviour is supplied by the browser.
- If a service-start link is styled as a button, retain an href and use the official start-button markup.
- Do not encode action meaning through colour alone; the label must describe the consequence.
- Preserve the official focus treatment and do not remove the visible focus indicator.

#### Content rules

- Write labels in sentence case.
- Start with a verb and describe the action, such as “Continue”, “Save and continue”, or “Delete account”.
- Avoid vague labels such as “Submit” when a more specific action can be named.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.success`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.text`

#### HTML examples

##### Default submit button

```html
<button type="submit" class="govuk-button" data-module="govuk-button">
  Save and continue
</button>
```

##### Secondary button

```html
<button type="submit" class="govuk-button govuk-button--secondary" data-module="govuk-button">
  Find address
</button>
```

##### Warning button

```html
<button type="submit" class="govuk-button govuk-button--warning" data-module="govuk-button">
  Delete account
</button>
```

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/button/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/button)

### Character count

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Character count when a textarea has a genuine maximum number of characters or words that users need help meeting.

#### When to use

- Use when a back-end or downstream process imposes a real maximum and users benefit from seeing what remains.
- Choose either a character limit or word limit that matches the actual validation rule.

#### When not to use

- Do not impose a limit only to keep stored answers or layouts convenient.
- Use an ordinary Textarea if users do not need a strict maximum.

#### Anatomy

- **Character-count form group (required):** The container carries data-module and one max-length or max-words configuration.
- **Textarea (required):** A govuk-textarea govuk-js-character-count control has a label and references the count message.
- **Count message (required):** A uniquely identified hint provides the limit before enhancement and live remaining-count updates after enhancement.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Character limit | `div` | `govuk-character-count` | A limit defined in characters using data-maxlength. |
| Word limit | `div` | `govuk-character-count` | A limit defined in words using data-maxwords. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise the official govuk-character-count module and keep its govuk-js hook classes.
- Without JavaScript, show a static message describing the maximum and enforce the same rule on the server.
- Do not rely on the HTML maxlength attribute as the only validation because it can prevent users from seeing how much they exceeded the limit.

#### Accessibility contract

- Associate the visible label and add the message ID to aria-describedby.
- Use the module's throttled screen-reader announcements rather than creating a live update for every keystroke.
- On error, link the error message and explain how far the answer exceeds the limit.

#### Content rules

- Tell users the maximum before they type and whether it counts words or characters.
- Phrase remaining and exceeded messages consistently and localise all module messages.
- Do not encourage users to fill the full allowance.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.secondary-text`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.focus`

#### HTML examples

##### Ten-character limit

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group govuk-character-count" data-module="govuk-character-count" data-maxlength="10">
  <label class="govuk-label" for="more-detail">Can you provide more detail?</label>
  <textarea class="govuk-textarea govuk-js-character-count" id="more-detail" name="moreDetail" rows="5" aria-describedby="more-detail-info"></textarea>
  <div id="more-detail-info" class="govuk-hint govuk-character-count__message">You can enter up to 10 characters</div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/character-count/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/character-count)

### Checkboxes

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use checkboxes when users can select any number of options from a visible set, including none when allowed.

#### When to use

- Use when zero, one or several answers may be valid and the options can be shown together.
- Use a divider and explicit exclusive “None” option only when users must state that no listed choice applies.

#### When not to use

- Use radios or a select when exactly one answer is required.
- Do not use checkboxes for acceptance of hidden terms or to trigger immediate navigation.

#### Anatomy

- **Fieldset and legend (required):** A fieldset groups the question and every checkbox.
- **Checkbox group (required):** A govuk-checkboxes container carries the enhancement hook.
- **Checkbox items (required):** Each native input has a unique ID, shared name where appropriate, value and associated label.
- **Conditional content:** A checkbox may control a uniquely identified conditional region through the official module.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-checkboxes` | Most checkbox questions. |
| Small | `div` | `govuk-checkboxes`, `govuk-checkboxes--small` | A compact expert interface after confirming smaller controls remain usable. |
| Conditional reveal | `input` | `govuk-checkboxes__input` | Reveal a small follow-up field directly related to a selected answer. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise govuk-checkboxes when using conditional content or exclusive options.
- Without JavaScript, conditional content remains available and the server validates whether it is required.
- Do not conditionally reveal another set of checkboxes or complex content; take users to a new page instead.
- Retain checked values after validation errors.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use native checkbox inputs inside a fieldset with a visible legend.
- Associate every label, hint, error and conditional region using unique IDs and official attributes.
- Never make a preselected checkbox the default unless it represents a genuine, non-coercive default.

#### Content rules

- Make it clear that users can select all that apply.
- Write options as distinct, concise answers that make sense with the legend.
- Use positive wording and avoid overlapping options.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.error`

#### HTML examples

##### Nationality choices

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group">
  <fieldset class="govuk-fieldset">
    <legend class="govuk-fieldset__legend">What is your nationality?</legend>
    <div class="govuk-checkboxes" data-module="govuk-checkboxes">
      <div class="govuk-checkboxes__item"><input class="govuk-checkboxes__input" id="nationality-british" name="nationality" type="checkbox" value="british"><label class="govuk-label govuk-checkboxes__label" for="nationality-british">British</label></div>
      <div class="govuk-checkboxes__item"><input class="govuk-checkboxes__input" id="nationality-irish" name="nationality" type="checkbox" value="irish"><label class="govuk-label govuk-checkboxes__label" for="nationality-irish">Irish</label></div>
    </div>
  </fieldset>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/checkboxes/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/checkboxes)

### Cookie banner

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the Cookie banner to ask for consent to non-essential cookies and confirm the choice without blocking access to the service.

#### When to use

- Use when a service sets analytics, advertising or other non-essential cookies that require a user choice.
- Show the banner until the user accepts or rejects non-essential cookies, then show a short confirmation message.

#### When not to use

- Do not ask for consent for cookies that are strictly necessary to provide the service.
- Do not prevent users from accessing the service while waiting for a decision.

#### Anatomy

- **Region (required):** A labelled region contains the current cookie message and uses data-nosnippet.
- **Heading and explanation (required):** A concise heading and body explain which optional cookies are requested and why.
- **Choice controls (required):** Equivalent accept and reject buttons are accompanied by a cookie-preferences link.
- **Confirmation message:** After a choice, a replacement message confirms it and can be dismissed.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Consent question | `div` | `govuk-cookie-banner` | Ask the user to accept or reject non-essential cookies. |
| Choice confirmation | `div` | `govuk-cookie-banner`, `govuk-cookie-banner__message` | Confirm a stored cookie choice and provide a way to hide the message. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Application code must store the preference, apply it before setting non-essential cookies and replace the question with a confirmation message.
- Both accept and reject actions must work without client-side JavaScript, for example as ordinary form submissions.
- Do not re-display the question on every page after the service has stored a valid preference.

#### Accessibility contract

- Give the region a concise accessible name such as “Cookie banner”.
- Make accept and reject actions equally prominent and keyboard operable.
- Move focus only when testing shows it helps; do not unexpectedly trap or steal focus.

#### Content rules

- Name the service and explain the purpose of the optional cookies in plain language.
- Use explicit action labels such as “Accept analytics cookies” and “Reject analytics cookies”.
- Link to a page where users can review and change their preference.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.body-background`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.spacing.static.4`

#### HTML examples

##### Consent question

```html
<div class="govuk-cookie-banner" data-nosnippet role="region" aria-label="Cookie banner">
  <div class="govuk-cookie-banner__message govuk-width-container">
    <h2 class="govuk-cookie-banner__heading govuk-heading-m">Cookies on Example service</h2>
    <div class="govuk-cookie-banner__content"><p class="govuk-body">We use analytics cookies to understand how you use the service.</p></div>
    <div class="govuk-button-group">
      <button class="govuk-button" data-module="govuk-button" type="submit" name="cookies" value="accept">Accept analytics cookies</button>
      <button class="govuk-button" data-module="govuk-button" type="submit" name="cookies" value="reject">Reject analytics cookies</button>
      <a class="govuk-link" href="/cookies">View cookie preferences</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/cookie-banner/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/cookie-banner)

### Date input

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Date input to collect a memorable or document-based date as separate day, month and year fields.

#### When to use

- Use for dates users know or can copy from a document, such as date of birth or passport issue date.
- Use an example hint in the order expected by the service.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for dates users need to choose from a calendar, such as an appointment slot.
- Do not use a single unstructured field when the service needs day, month and year separately.
- Do not use input type=number because its interaction and formatting are unsuitable for date parts.

#### Anatomy

- **Fieldset and legend (required):** The date question groups its parts and references the example hint.
- **Date-input group (required):** A uniquely identified govuk-date-input contains the ordered parts.
- **Day, month and year inputs (required):** Each part has its own label, text input, numeric input mode, width and submitted name.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Day, month and year | `div` | `govuk-date-input` | A complete date in UK service order. |
| Error | `input` | `govuk-date-input__input`, `govuk-input--error` | Highlight only the invalid parts where possible and provide one specific group error. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The component requires no GOV.UK JavaScript.
- Parse and validate the three submitted strings on the server, including incomplete, impossible and context-invalid dates.
- Retain entered values and mark only affected parts when redisplaying an error.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use the fieldset, legend, role=group and unique labels shown in official markup.
- Reference the group hint and error from the fieldset and preserve visible focus on each part.
- Use inputmode=numeric while keeping type=text so users can enter leading zeroes and avoid number-input controls.

#### Content rules

- Ask which date is required in the legend.
- Use a realistic example such as “For example, 31 3 1980” without punctuation that suggests a different format.
- Write errors for missing parts, invalid dates and dates outside the allowed context.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`

#### HTML examples

##### Date of birth

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group"><fieldset class="govuk-fieldset" role="group" aria-describedby="dob-hint"><legend class="govuk-fieldset__legend">What is your date of birth?</legend><div id="dob-hint" class="govuk-hint">For example, 31 3 1980</div><div class="govuk-date-input" id="dob"><div class="govuk-date-input__item"><label class="govuk-label govuk-date-input__label" for="dob-day">Day</label><input class="govuk-input govuk-date-input__input govuk-input--width-2" id="dob-day" name="dobDay" type="text" inputmode="numeric"></div><div class="govuk-date-input__item"><label class="govuk-label govuk-date-input__label" for="dob-month">Month</label><input class="govuk-input govuk-date-input__input govuk-input--width-2" id="dob-month" name="dobMonth" type="text" inputmode="numeric"></div><div class="govuk-date-input__item"><label class="govuk-label govuk-date-input__label" for="dob-year">Year</label><input class="govuk-input govuk-date-input__input govuk-input--width-4" id="dob-year" name="dobYear" type="text" inputmode="numeric"></div></div></fieldset></div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/date-input/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/date-input)

### Details

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use details to let users reveal optional supporting information without distracting from the main task.

#### When to use

- Use for optional help or additional context that only some users need.
- Use when the summary alone clearly explains what will be revealed.

#### When not to use

- Do not hide information most users need to understand or complete the task.
- Do not hide validation errors, eligibility conditions or important consequences.
- Do not use several details components when a clearer page structure would be easier to scan.

#### Anatomy

- **Details element (required):** The native details element provides disclosure behaviour without GOV.UK JavaScript.
- **Summary (required):** A native summary contains a short, descriptive govuk-details__summary-text label.
- **Details text (required):** The revealed content sits in govuk-details__text.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Closed by default | `details` | `govuk-details` | Optional supporting content that is not required immediately. |
| Open by default | `details` | `govuk-details` | An exceptional case where the native open attribute is justified by the current context. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Use the browser's native details and summary disclosure; no GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
- Do not replace summary with a generic div or custom click handler.
- Content remains available in browsers that expose the native element without CSS.

#### Accessibility contract

- Keep the native elements and visible focus treatment.
- Make the summary meaningful when read independently and avoid duplicate summaries on a page.
- Ensure revealed interactive content follows the summary in a logical keyboard order.

#### Content rules

- Write the summary as a concise label for the hidden content, such as “Help with nationality”.
- Keep the revealed answer focused and move essential instructions into the main page content.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.text`

#### HTML examples

##### Optional help

```html
<details class="govuk-details">
  <summary class="govuk-details__summary">
    <span class="govuk-details__summary-text">Help with nationality</span>
  </summary>
  <div class="govuk-details__text">Tell us the nationality shown on your passport.</div>
</details>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/details/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/details)

### Error message

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use an error message next to an invalid field to explain what went wrong and how the user can correct it.

#### When to use

- Show beside every field that fails validation after the user submits or leaves the relevant step.
- Use with the matching component error state and, for page-level validation, an error summary.

#### When not to use

- Do not use an error message for hints, warnings or validation that has not occurred.
- Do not show only a generic page error while leaving the affected field unidentified.

#### Anatomy

- **Message container (required):** A uniquely identified govuk-error-message is placed immediately before the invalid control.
- **Hidden error prefix (required):** A govuk-visually-hidden prefix makes the error context explicit without relying on red styling.
- **Corrective message (required):** Specific text tells the user what to enter or change.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `p` | `govuk-error-message` | A field-level validation error. |
| Localised prefix | `p` | `govuk-error-message` | A page whose language requires a translated hidden Error prefix. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Add the message ID to the invalid control's aria-describedby after any hint ID.
- Redisplay the user's value unless it is unsafe to do so and keep server-side validation authoritative.
- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use matching IDs so assistive technology announces hint text followed by the error.
- Apply the component's visual error class as well; never communicate the error through colour alone.
- Move focus to the error summary for a submitted page with multiple or page-level errors.

#### Content rules

- Use concise instructions such as “Enter a date in the correct format”.
- Do not use vague text such as “Invalid entry”, blame the user, or repeat the word Error in the visible message.
- Use consistent wording between the error summary link and the field message.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`

#### HTML examples

##### Field error message

```html
<p id="passport-issued-error" class="govuk-error-message">
  <span class="govuk-visually-hidden">Error:</span> Enter the date your passport was issued
</p>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-message/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/error-message)

### Error summary

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the Error summary at the top of a page to list validation errors and link each message to the field that needs attention.

#### When to use

- Use after server-side or client-side validation fails on a page with user inputs.
- Place it near the top of main content and repeat each error beside its field.

#### When not to use

- Do not use as the only indication that a field has an error.
- Do not use for system failures or service-wide status messages; use an appropriate error page or notification instead.

#### Anatomy

- **Summary container (required):** A GOV.UK JavaScript module contains an alert region.
- **Title (required):** A heading identifies that the page contains a problem.
- **Error list (required):** Each concise message links to the related input, fieldset legend or other appropriate target.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-error-summary` | Summarise one or more validation errors on the current page. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise the govuk-error-summary module so it can move focus to the summary when appropriate after validation.
- Each link must target the relevant form control; for grouped controls, target the first control unless research supports a better focus target.
- Keep server-side validation authoritative even when adding client-side validation.

#### Accessibility contract

- Put the summary inside main content and keep it visible in the document without JavaScript.
- Use matching text in the summary and the inline error so users can connect them.
- Do not rely on red colour or focus movement alone to announce errors.

#### Content rules

- Use a standard title such as “There is a problem”.
- Write messages that explain what happened and how to fix it, without blaming the user.
- Do not include the word “Error” before every list item.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`

#### HTML examples

##### Validation summary

```html
<div class="govuk-error-summary" data-module="govuk-error-summary">
  <div role="alert">
    <h2 class="govuk-error-summary__title">There is a problem</h2>
    <div class="govuk-error-summary__body">
      <ul class="govuk-list govuk-error-summary__list">
        <li><a href="#email">Enter an email address</a></li>
      </ul>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-summary/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/error-summary)

### Exit this page

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Exit this page in sensitive services when viewing the page could put someone at risk and they may need to leave immediately.

#### When to use

- Use only when sensitive page content could place a user in danger if another person sees it.
- Use it as part of the complete GOV.UK pattern for leaving a page quickly, including the secondary hidden exit link and service-level safety decisions.

#### When not to use

- Do not use as a normal close, cancel, sign-out or back control.
- Do not assume the component clears browser history, hides network activity or guarantees a user’s safety.

#### Anatomy

- **Exit container (required):** The component module coordinates pointer, keyboard and repeated-key activation.
- **Warning action (required):** A warning-styled link has button semantics and navigates to a safer neutral destination.
- **Hidden emergency context (required):** Visually hidden text makes the urgency clear without lengthening the visible label.
- **Secondary exit link:** The complete pattern includes an early hidden link to the same destination for assistive-technology users.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `a` | `govuk-button`, `govuk-button--warning`, `govuk-exit-this-page__button` | A prominent emergency exit action near the top of a sensitive page. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise govuk-exit-this-page so the button supports the documented rapid keyboard gesture and enhanced loading feedback.
- The ordinary href must navigate immediately when JavaScript is unavailable.
- Choose a neutral, non-personalised destination and consider clearing sensitive application session data before redirecting.

#### Accessibility contract

- Position the action early in the page inside the width container and keep its focus treatment visible.
- Provide the companion hidden exit link described by the full pattern, pointing to the same destination.
- Test wording, placement and destination with people who face the relevant safety risk.

#### Content rules

- Keep the visible label direct, normally “Exit this page”.
- Use visually hidden context such as “Emergency” where it makes the action clearer to screen-reader users.
- Explain any limitations or additional safety advice elsewhere in the service without delaying the exit action.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`

#### HTML examples

##### Emergency exit action

```html
<div class="govuk-exit-this-page" data-module="govuk-exit-this-page">
  <a href="https://www.bbc.co.uk/weather" role="button" draggable="false" class="govuk-button govuk-button--warning govuk-exit-this-page__button govuk-js-exit-this-page-button" data-module="govuk-button" rel="nofollow noreferrer">
    <span class="govuk-visually-hidden">Emergency</span> Exit this page
  </a>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/exit-this-page/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/exit-this-page)

### Feedback

**Status:** Trial  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the Feedback component to give users a consistent, low-distraction route for sharing their experience of a service.

#### When to use

- Use on as many service pages as practical when the team has a feedback route it monitors.
- Place immediately before the footer so it remains available without distracting from the current task.

#### When not to use

- Do not use when feedback is not reviewed or cannot influence the service.
- Do not use it as a replacement for a support route when users need help completing a task.

#### Anatomy

- **Feedback region (required):** A govuk-feedback container uses the standard width and grid.
- **Title (required):** A configurable heading identifies the invitation.
- **Message and link (required):** Brief body copy explains why feedback is useful and links to the feedback route.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-feedback`, `govuk-width-container` | The service-wide invitation shown before the footer. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The component has no GOV.UK JavaScript behaviour; its link must work without JavaScript.
- In the Nunjucks page template, place it in footerStart so document order remains consistent.
- Treat this Trial component as changeable and review it on every GOV.UK Frontend update.

#### Accessibility contract

- Set headingLevel so the title fits the page's heading hierarchy.
- Make the feedback link purpose clear from its text and surrounding sentence.
- Distinguish feedback from urgent help and provide an accessible support route elsewhere.

#### Content rules

- Explain why feedback is requested and what the team will do with it.
- Where useful, say how long providing feedback will take and distinguish it from support.
- Use a direct label such as “Give us your feedback”.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.surface-background`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.layout.page-width`

#### HTML examples

##### Service feedback invitation

```html
<div class="govuk-feedback govuk-width-container">
  <div class="govuk-grid-row">
    <div class="govuk-grid-column-two-thirds">
      <h2 class="govuk-feedback__title">Help us improve this service</h2>
      <div class="govuk-feedback__body">
        <p class="govuk-body">Tell us about your experience using this service. <a href="/feedback" class="govuk-link">Give us your feedback</a></p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/feedback/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/feedback)

### Fieldset

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a fieldset and legend to group related form controls under one question or shared label.

#### When to use

- Use to group related controls such as a radio group, checkbox group, date input or multi-part address.
- Use a legend as the page heading when the group is the page's main question.

#### When not to use

- Do not use a fieldset around a single, independently labelled text input.
- Do not use visual spacing alone to imply that controls belong to one question.

#### Anatomy

- **Fieldset (required):** The native fieldset contains every control belonging to the group.
- **Legend (required):** The first child is a clear govuk-fieldset__legend that labels the entire group.
- **Grouped controls (required):** Each child control still has its own label where required.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default legend | `fieldset` | `govuk-fieldset` | A related group within a larger page. |
| Legend as page heading | `legend` | `govuk-fieldset__legend`, `govuk-fieldset__legend--l` | The fieldset question is the page's primary heading and contains an h1 with govuk-fieldset__heading. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required for the fieldset itself.
- Keep the legend as the first meaningful child so browsers announce it with each grouped control.
- Place group hint and error content in the related form group and link it using the component's documented IDs.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use native fieldset and legend rather than role=group when native grouping is available.
- Do not leave the legend empty or hide it when users need the group question.
- Avoid nested fieldsets unless the question hierarchy remains clear in tested assistive technologies.

#### Content rules

- Write the legend as a direct question or concise group label.
- Do not repeat the same wording in a separate heading and legend when the legend can be the heading.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.spacing.static.3`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`

#### HTML examples

##### Address group

```html
<fieldset class="govuk-fieldset">
  <legend class="govuk-fieldset__legend">What is your address?</legend>
  <label class="govuk-label" for="address-line-1">Address line 1</label>
  <input class="govuk-input" id="address-line-1" name="addressLine1" type="text">
</fieldset>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/fieldset/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/fieldset)

### File upload

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use file upload when users must select and submit one or more files from their device.

#### When to use

- Use only when a file is necessary and the service cannot obtain the information another way.
- Explain accepted formats, size limits and whether multiple files are allowed before the control.

#### When not to use

- Do not ask for a file when users can provide a short answer directly in the service.
- Do not rely on the accept attribute or client-side checks as authoritative validation.

#### Anatomy

- **Form group (required):** Groups the visible label, optional hint, optional error and file input.
- **Label (required):** A label associated by for and id tells users what to upload.
- **Native file input (required):** An input type=file keeps browser and assistive-technology selection behaviour.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Single file | `input` | `govuk-file-upload` | Upload one required file. |
| Error | `input` | `govuk-file-upload`, `govuk-file-upload--error` | Redisplay after a missing, invalid or failed upload with a linked error message. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Submit using a form encoding that supports files and validate the received file on the server.
- Handle missing, oversized, unsupported and malicious files safely and explain recoverable errors.
- The base file input does not require GOV.UK JavaScript.

#### Accessibility contract

- Keep the native input and an associated visible label.
- Reference hint and error IDs with aria-describedby in that order.
- Do not make drag-and-drop the only way to select a file.

#### Content rules

- Name the document or evidence required rather than using only “Upload a file”.
- State accepted formats, maximum size and how to provide an alternative.
- Error messages must say whether the user needs a different file, format or size.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`

#### HTML examples

##### Single supporting document

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group">
  <label class="govuk-label" for="evidence">Upload your supporting evidence</label>
  <div id="evidence-hint" class="govuk-hint">The file must be a PDF, JPG or PNG smaller than 10MB.</div>
  <input class="govuk-file-upload" id="evidence" name="evidence" type="file" aria-describedby="evidence-hint">
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/file-upload/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/file-upload)

### Generic header

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the Generic header to give a public-sector service a clear branded header when it is not entitled to use the GOV.UK crown and logotype.

#### When to use

- Use for services outside the GOV.UK proposition that want a compatible GOV.UK Frontend page structure without GOV.UK identity assets.
- Use a concise organisation or service name as the homepage link.

#### When not to use

- Do not use it as an imitation GOV.UK header by adding the GOV.UK crown, logotype or protected identity styling.
- Do not replace the official GOV.UK header with this component when the service is authorised and required to use the GOV.UK identity.

#### Anatomy

- **Header container (required):** A full-width header contains an aligned GOV.UK width container.
- **Homepage link (required):** A prominent text link names the service or organisation and returns to its home page.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-generic-header` | A non-GOV.UK service with a short text identity. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The Generic header requires no GOV.UK JavaScript and the homepage control is an ordinary link.
- Keep the link destination stable and preserve standard browser link behaviour.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use a real link with a visible accessible name and sufficient contrast.
- Keep the text identity legible at narrow widths and high zoom.
- Do not communicate the service identity through an image or colour alone.

#### Content rules

- Use the official public name of the service or organisation.
- Keep the name short enough to wrap predictably on small screens.
- Do not add the words GOV.UK or a crown mark unless use has been explicitly authorised.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.body-background`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.layout.page-width`

#### HTML examples

##### Text identity

```html
<div class="govuk-generic-header">
  <div class="govuk-generic-header__container govuk-width-container">
    <div class="govuk-generic-header__logo"><a href="/" class="govuk-generic-header__homepage-link">Example service</a></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/generic-header/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/generic-header)

### GOV.UK footer

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the official GOV.UK footer on authorised GOV.UK services for service links, licensing and Crown copyright information.

#### When to use

- Use the official footer on services that are part of GOV.UK and authorised to use its identity and standard licensing statements.
- Add only useful service links, grouped into navigation sections when there are enough links to justify them.

#### When not to use

- Do not use Crown identity or licensing claims for content that is not covered by them.
- Do not recreate or redistribute crown and licensing artwork from these documentation records; consume the official GOV.UK Frontend component and assets.

#### Anatomy

- **Footer container (required):** A semantic footer aligns its content to the GOV.UK width container.
- **Navigation sections:** Optional headings and lists group useful service links.
- **Meta links:** A compact list contains service policies and other secondary destinations.
- **Licence and copyright (required):** Official assets and wording describe applicable content licensing and Crown copyright.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `footer` | `govuk-footer` | Licence, copyright and a small set of meta links. |
| With navigation | `footer` | `govuk-footer` | Add organised link columns when a service has several persistent destinations. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The Footer requires no GOV.UK JavaScript and all destinations must be ordinary links.
- Use the official template or macro so identity, licence markup and assets stay aligned with the pinned release.
- Do not copy protected identity SVG data into framework adapters or generated DESIGN.md files.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use a semantic footer landmark and heading levels that fit the surrounding page.
- Give each navigation group a clear heading and keep link text descriptive.
- Preserve the official link focus treatments and accessible handling of decorative assets.

#### Content rules

- Include only links users reasonably expect to find across the whole service.
- Keep official licence and copyright wording unchanged unless legal guidance for the service requires a different statement.
- Do not imply Crown ownership or Open Government Licence coverage where it does not apply.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.template-background`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.layout.page-width`

#### HTML examples

##### Official macro required

```html
<!-- Render the GOV.UK Frontend footer macro/component from the pinned release. -->
<footer class="govuk-footer">
  <div class="govuk-width-container">
    <div class="govuk-footer__meta"><div class="govuk-footer__meta-item govuk-footer__meta-item--grow">
      <!-- Official licence and Crown copyright markup and supplied assets go here. -->
    </div></div>
  </div>
</footer>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/footer/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/footer)

### GOV.UK header

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the official GOV.UK header on authorised GOV.UK services to identify the site and link consistently to the GOV.UK homepage.

#### When to use

- Use the official component for services that are part of GOV.UK and authorised to display its crown and logotype.
- Pair it with Service navigation when the service needs a service name or service-level links.

#### When not to use

- Do not use the GOV.UK crown or logotype for a service outside the GOV.UK proposition or without identity approval.
- Do not recreate, redraw or substitute the protected identity asset from these documentation records; use the official GOV.UK Frontend component and assets.

#### Anatomy

- **Header (required):** The GOV.UK header component establishes the official site identity.
- **Width container (required):** The inner content aligns with the page grid.
- **GOV.UK homepage link (required):** The official crown and logotype link to the GOV.UK homepage with the supplied accessible name.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `header` | `govuk-header` | The standard GOV.UK site identity above Service navigation or main content. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The current GOV.UK header itself requires no component JavaScript; initialise any separate Service navigation beneath it.
- Use the official template or macro so identity markup and assets stay aligned with the pinned GOV.UK Frontend release.
- Do not inline an invented or extracted logo in framework adapters.

#### Accessibility contract

- Preserve the official accessible name, link semantics and focus treatment supplied by GOV.UK Frontend.
- Keep the header readable at high zoom and do not place application content over the identity.
- Avoid duplicate GOV.UK homepage links with the same accessible name in the header.

#### Content rules

- Do not alter the GOV.UK logotype text, crown or relationship between them.
- Put the service name and service-level links in Service navigation, not inside a custom header imitation.
- Follow the GOV.UK identity and domain guidance before publication.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.brand`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.layout.page-width`

#### HTML examples

##### Official macro required

