```html
<!-- Render the GOV.UK Frontend header macro/component from the pinned release. -->
<header class="govuk-header">
  <div class="govuk-header__container govuk-width-container">
    <div class="govuk-header__logo"><!-- Official GOV.UK homepage link and supplied logotype asset go here. --></div>
  </div>
</header>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/header/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/header)

### Inset text

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use inset text to distinguish a short block of supporting information from the content around it.

#### When to use

- Use for important supplementary information that users should notice but that is not a warning or success state.
- Use for a short block that benefits from visual separation within the flow of the page.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for warnings about serious consequences; use Warning text.
- Do not use for successful completion; use a Panel where appropriate.
- Do not place most of a page inside inset text.

#### Anatomy

- **Inset container (required):** A govuk-inset-text container provides the reviewed left border and spacing.
- **Supporting content (required):** Concise text or simple semantic content explains the supporting point.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-inset-text` | A short supporting block on the standard page background. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The component has no JavaScript behaviour and remains ordinary document content without CSS.
- Keep it in the reading order at the point where its information is relevant.

#### Accessibility contract

- The left border is decorative; the wording must carry the full meaning.
- Add semantic headings, lists or links inside only when the content requires them.
- Do not use colour or placement alone to indicate urgency.

#### Content rules

- Keep the message concise and directly related to the surrounding task.
- Use ordinary sentence case and avoid a heading unless it helps users scan a longer inset.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.border.standard`
- `govuk.spacing.static.3`

#### HTML examples

##### Processing-time information

```html
<div class="govuk-inset-text">
  It can take up to 8 weeks to register a lasting power of attorney.
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/inset-text/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/inset-text)

### Language navigation

**Status:** Trial  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Language navigation to let users identify the current language and switch to equivalent versions offered by the service.

#### When to use

- Use when the service offers equivalent content or journeys in more than one language.
- Keep the switcher consistently placed and preserve journey state where the service can do so safely.

#### When not to use

- Do not show a language as available when the linked page or journey is incomplete.
- Do not use country flags to represent languages.

#### Anatomy

- **Language navigation landmark (required):** A nav has a localised aria-label describing the language choice.
- **Language list (required):** A list contains one item for each offered language.
- **Current language (required):** Non-link text has aria-current=true and an accurate lang attribute.
- **Alternative links (required):** Each link uses rel=alternate, lang and hreflang for the target language.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `nav` | `govuk-language-navigation` | A small language set on a standard background. |
| Inverse | `nav` | `govuk-language-navigation`, `govuk-language-navigation--inverse` | A supported dark-background location with verified contrast. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The component requires no GOV.UK JavaScript and all alternative links must be ordinary href navigation.
- Retain relevant user data across language changes only where privacy, validation and service design allow it.
- Review this Trial component when updating GOV.UK Frontend because its guidance or API may change.

#### Accessibility contract

- Write each language name in that language and set lang so assistive technology pronounces it correctly.
- Set dir on items when scripts have different writing directions.
- Localise the navigation label and any visually hidden language-description text.

#### Content rules

- Use the native name for each language, for example “Cymraeg”.
- Do not abbreviate language names unless research shows the abbreviation is understood.
- Keep equivalent pages aligned so switching language does not unexpectedly change the task.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`

#### HTML examples

##### English and Welsh navigation

```html
<nav class="govuk-language-navigation" aria-label="Language">
  <ul class="govuk-language-navigation__list">
    <li class="govuk-language-navigation__list-item"><span class="govuk-language-navigation__text" aria-current="true" lang="en">English</span></li>
    <li class="govuk-language-navigation__list-item"><a class="govuk-language-navigation__link" href="/cy" rel="alternate" lang="cy" hreflang="cy">Cymraeg</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/language-navigation/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/language-navigation)

### Notification banner

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the Notification banner to tell users about an important change or the successful result of an action.

#### When to use

- Use for important information that applies to the current page or for a success message after an action.
- Put the banner after breadcrumbs or back link and before the main page heading.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for validation errors; use the Error summary and inline Error message.
- Do not use instead of a confirmation page when the completed transaction needs a reference or durable record.

#### Anatomy

- **Labelled region (required):** A region references the banner title with aria-labelledby.
- **Banner title (required):** A compact heading identifies an important or successful notification.
- **Content (required):** The content states the message and can include a relevant link.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Important | `div` | `govuk-notification-banner` | Important information that is not a success confirmation. |
| Success | `div` | `govuk-notification-banner`, `govuk-notification-banner--success` | Confirm a successful action on the next page. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise the govuk-notification-banner module; it manages focus for a success banner unless auto-focus is explicitly disabled.
- Render important information as a region and success feedback as an alert using the official macro options.
- The full message must remain available without client-side JavaScript.

#### Accessibility contract

- Give every banner title a unique id and reference it from aria-labelledby.
- Use the success role and automatic focus sparingly so screen-reader users are notified without repeated interruptions.
- Keep links descriptive and make meaning independent of colour.

#### Content rules

- Use “Important” for the default title and “Success” for a successful outcome unless a clearer short label is needed.
- Lead with what changed or what the user completed.
- Include only actions directly related to the notification.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.brand`
- `govuk.color.success`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.focus`

#### HTML examples

##### Important notification

```html
<div class="govuk-notification-banner" role="region" aria-labelledby="notice-title" data-module="govuk-notification-banner">
  <div class="govuk-notification-banner__header"><h2 class="govuk-notification-banner__title" id="notice-title">Important</h2></div>
  <div class="govuk-notification-banner__content"><p class="govuk-notification-banner__heading">Your application deadline has changed.</p></div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/notification-banner/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/notification-banner)

### Pagination

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use pagination to help users move through a collection split across several pages.

#### When to use

- Use when a long result set or collection is meaningfully divided into pages.
- Use block-style previous and next links for content pages where destination labels help orientation.

#### When not to use

- Do not paginate a short list that is easier to scan on one page.
- Do not use pagination to represent steps in a transaction.

#### Anatomy

- **Pagination navigation (required):** A nav landmark has a concise pagination label.
- **Previous and next links:** Directional links use rel=prev or rel=next and hidden “page” context.
- **Page list:** Numbered links include accessible page labels and identify the current page.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Numbered | `nav` | `govuk-pagination` | A results collection where users may move to a particular page. |
| Block previous and next | `nav` | `govuk-pagination`, `govuk-pagination--block` | Sequential content where descriptive previous and next labels help users. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Every destination is a normal server-resolvable link; no GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
- Omit previous on the first page and next on the last page instead of rendering disabled links.
- Preserve active filters and sorting in pagination URLs.

#### Accessibility contract

- Set aria-current="page" on the current page link.
- Give numbered links accessible names such as “Page 3”; hidden context distinguishes Previous page and Next page.
- Hide decorative arrow SVGs using aria-hidden and focusable=false.

#### Content rules

- Use “Previous” and “Next” consistently.
- For block navigation, add a concise label that names the destination content.
- Do not show every page number when a large range would become difficult to scan.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.border`

#### HTML examples

##### Previous and next links

```html
<nav class="govuk-pagination" aria-label="Pagination">
  <div class="govuk-pagination__prev"><a class="govuk-link govuk-pagination__link" href="?page=1" rel="prev"><span class="govuk-pagination__link-title">Previous<span class="govuk-visually-hidden"> page</span></span></a></div>
  <div class="govuk-pagination__next"><a class="govuk-link govuk-pagination__link" href="?page=3" rel="next"><span class="govuk-pagination__link-title">Next<span class="govuk-visually-hidden"> page</span></span></a></div>
</nav>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/pagination/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/pagination)

### Panel

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a panel to highlight the outcome of an important action, especially successful completion of a transaction.

#### When to use

- Use at the top of a confirmation page to tell users that they completed an important action.
- Include a reference number or other short result in the body when users must retain it.

#### When not to use

- Do not use a panel for routine information, warnings or validation errors.
- Do not rely on the panel as the entire confirmation page; follow it with what happens next.

#### Anatomy

- **Confirmation panel (required):** A govuk-panel govuk-panel--confirmation container carries the highlighted outcome.
- **Title (required):** A concise heading states the successful result and is normally the page h1.
- **Body:** Optional content shows a reference or another immediately important detail.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Confirmation | `div` | `govuk-panel`, `govuk-panel--confirmation` | The primary outcome at the start of a confirmation page. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
- Render the panel after the server has completed or authoritatively confirmed the action, not as an optimistic client-only state.
- Follow the panel with details about next steps, timing, records and support.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use an h1 for the confirmation title when it is the page's main heading.
- Ensure the result is explicit in text and not conveyed only by the green background.
- When navigation moves to the confirmation page, make the page title and heading identify the completed task.

#### Content rules

- State the outcome directly, such as “Application complete”.
- Label any reference number and make it easy to copy accurately.
- Do not use celebratory or vague copy that obscures what was completed.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.success`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`

#### HTML examples

##### Application confirmation

```html
<div class="govuk-panel govuk-panel--confirmation">
  <h1 class="govuk-panel__title">Application complete</h1>
  <div class="govuk-panel__body">Your reference number<br><strong>HDJ2123F</strong></div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/panel/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/panel)

### Password input

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use the Password input when users need to enter a password, with an optional progressively enhanced control to show or hide it.

#### When to use

- Use for a password used to create or access an account.
- Use the show or hide control when seeing the entered value helps users prevent mistakes.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for a one-time security code, memorable answer or other value that is not a password.
- Do not prevent password managers or pasting into the field.

#### Anatomy

- **Label (required):** A visible label is explicitly associated with the password field.
- **Password field (required):** A type=password input uses suitable autocomplete, spelling and capitalisation attributes.
- **Show or hide toggle:** A hidden-by-default button is revealed by GOV.UK JavaScript and controls the input.
- **Hint and error:** Instructions and validation feedback are referenced with aria-describedby.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `input` | `govuk-input`, `govuk-password-input__input`, `govuk-js-password-input-input` | A current or newly created password. |
| Error | `input` | `govuk-input`, `govuk-input--error`, `govuk-password-input__input` | A password field whose submitted value did not meet the stated requirement. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise the govuk-password-input module to reveal the toggle and switch the field type between password and text.
- The toggle updates its visible label and accessible name between show and hide states.
- Without JavaScript, the password field remains usable and the hidden toggle stays hidden.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use autocomplete=current-password for sign-in and autocomplete=new-password when creating or changing a password.
- Keep the field label visible and associate hint or error ids through aria-describedby.
- Allow browsers and assistive software to reveal, paste and fill passwords.

#### Content rules

- State password requirements before the field and describe only rules the service actually enforces.
- Use “Show” and “Hide” toggle labels with accessible names that include “password”.
- Error messages should identify the unmet requirement without reproducing the password.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.spacing.static.2`

#### HTML examples

##### Current password

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group govuk-password-input" data-module="govuk-password-input">
  <label class="govuk-label" for="password">Password</label>
  <div class="govuk-input__wrapper govuk-password-input__wrapper">
    <input class="govuk-input govuk-password-input__input govuk-js-password-input-input" id="password" name="password" type="password" spellcheck="false" autocomplete="current-password" autocapitalize="none">
    <button type="button" class="govuk-button govuk-button--secondary govuk-password-input__toggle govuk-js-password-input-toggle" data-module="govuk-button" aria-controls="password" aria-label="Show password" hidden>Show</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/password-input/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/password-input)

### Phase banner

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a phase banner to show that a service is in alpha or beta and give users a way to provide feedback.

#### When to use

- Use when a public service is genuinely in alpha or beta and users should understand its development status.
- Provide a working feedback route that the team monitors and can act on.

#### When not to use

- Do not use a phase banner as a substitute for explaining known limitations or service availability.
- Do not retain an alpha or beta label after the service no longer meets that lifecycle stage.

#### Anatomy

- **Banner container (required):** A govuk-phase-banner sits inside the standard width context near the top of the page.
- **Phase tag (required):** A GOV.UK Tag contains the current phase label.
- **Feedback message (required):** Short text explains that the service is developing and contains a feedback link.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Alpha | `div` | `govuk-phase-banner` | An alpha service being tested and iterated. |
| Beta | `div` | `govuk-phase-banner` | A beta service available to users while continuing to improve. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
- Place the banner consistently below the header or service navigation and before main content.
- The feedback link must work without JavaScript.

#### Accessibility contract

- The phase is visible text inside the tag rather than a colour-only badge.
- Use descriptive feedback-link text when the surrounding sentence would not be announced with it.
- Preserve link focus and visited-state behaviour.

#### Content rules

- Use the actual service phase label, usually “Alpha” or “Beta”.
- Keep the message short and explain that feedback helps improve the service.
- Link directly to the feedback mechanism rather than a generic homepage.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.spacing.static.2`

#### HTML examples

##### Alpha phase banner

```html
<div class="govuk-phase-banner">
  <p class="govuk-phase-banner__content">
    <strong class="govuk-tag govuk-phase-banner__content__tag">Alpha</strong>
    <span class="govuk-phase-banner__text">This is a new service – your <a href="/feedback" class="govuk-link">feedback</a> will help us to improve it.</span>
  </p>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/phase-banner/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/phase-banner)

### Radios

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use radios when users must choose exactly one option from a small, visible set.

#### When to use

- Use for one answer from a small set where seeing every option helps users compare.
- Use inline radios only for short, familiar binary choices such as Yes and No.

#### When not to use

- Use checkboxes when more than one answer may be selected.
- Use a select or autocomplete when the option set is too long to scan.
- Do not preselect an answer unless it is a genuine, safe default.

#### Anatomy

- **Fieldset and legend (required):** A fieldset groups the question and all radio options.
- **Radio group (required):** A govuk-radios container carries the enhancement hook.
- **Radio items (required):** Native inputs share one name and each has a unique ID, value and associated label.
- **Conditional content:** An option may reveal one small, directly related follow-up region.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stacked | `div` | `govuk-radios` | The default for most radio questions. |
| Inline | `div` | `govuk-radios`, `govuk-radios--inline` | Short binary choices such as Yes and No. |
| Small | `div` | `govuk-radios`, `govuk-radios--small` | A compact expert interface after testing target size and usability. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise govuk-radios when using conditional content.
- Without JavaScript, conditional content remains visible and server validation remains authoritative.
- Do not reveal complex questions or another radio group conditionally; use a new page.
- Retain the selected value after validation errors.

#### Accessibility contract

- Use native radio inputs inside a fieldset with a visible legend.
- Associate labels, hints, errors and conditional content using unique IDs and official attributes.
- Ensure options remain understandable in source order and with styling removed.

#### Content rules

- Write mutually exclusive, non-overlapping options that complete the legend's question.
- Use a divider such as “or” only to separate a distinct final alternative.
- Keep labels concise and add item hints only where necessary.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.error`

#### HTML examples

##### Yes or no

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group"><fieldset class="govuk-fieldset"><legend class="govuk-fieldset__legend">Have you changed your name?</legend><div class="govuk-radios govuk-radios--inline" data-module="govuk-radios"><div class="govuk-radios__item"><input class="govuk-radios__input" id="changed-name" name="changedName" type="radio" value="yes"><label class="govuk-label govuk-radios__label" for="changed-name">Yes</label></div><div class="govuk-radios__item"><input class="govuk-radios__input" id="changed-name-2" name="changedName" type="radio" value="no"><label class="govuk-label govuk-radios__label" for="changed-name-2">No</label></div></div></fieldset></div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/radios)

### Select

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a select when users must choose one option from a familiar list that is too long for radios.

#### When to use

- Use for one choice from a moderately long list whose options users already understand.
- Order options predictably and select a value only when a genuine default exists.

#### When not to use

- Use radios for a small set because all options remain visible.
- Use an accessible autocomplete for a very long list such as countries when users benefit from search.
- Do not use a select for multiple choices unless research supports the native multiple-select interaction.

#### Anatomy

- **Form group (required):** Groups label, optional hint, optional error and select.
- **Label (required):** A visible label is associated using for and id.
- **Native select (required):** A govuk-select contains semantic option elements and submits the selected value.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `select` | `govuk-select` | A single choice from a familiar option set. |
| Error | `select` | `govuk-select`, `govuk-select--error` | Redisplay an invalid or missing selection with a linked error message. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Use the native select without replacing its keyboard and platform behaviour; no GOV.UK JavaScript is required.
- Validate the submitted value on the server against the allowed options.
- Retain the user's selection after a validation error.

#### Accessibility contract

- Associate one visible label and reference hint and error IDs with aria-describedby.
- Do not use size or multiple attributes without testing their more complex interaction.
- Avoid a disabled placeholder as the only instruction; use a label and hint.

#### Content rules

- Write a clear question in the label and concise option labels.
- Sort alphabetically, numerically or by a user-understood priority.
- Do not preselect an answer merely to avoid a blank value.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`

#### HTML examples

##### Country selection

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group">
  <label class="govuk-label" for="country">Country</label>
  <select class="govuk-select" id="country" name="country">
    <option value="">Select a country</option>
    <option value="england">England</option>
    <option value="scotland">Scotland</option>
    <option value="wales">Wales</option>
  </select>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/select/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/select)

### Service navigation

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Service navigation beneath the GOV.UK header to show a service name and a small set of service-level navigation links.

#### When to use

- Use for a GOV.UK service that needs a visible service name, service navigation links, or both beneath the GOV.UK header.
- Keep navigation short and limited to persistent top-level destinations supported by user research.

#### When not to use

- Do not use to reproduce the GOV.UK global header or for page-level tabs and task navigation.
- Do not add a menu simply to fill the space when the service has no persistent top-level navigation.

#### Anatomy

- **Service container (required):** A GOV.UK module and width container align the service bar with page content.
- **Service name:** A link identifies and returns to the service home page.
- **Navigation landmark:** A labelled nav contains a short list of service destinations.
- **Responsive menu toggle:** A hidden-by-default button controls the navigation list on narrow screens after enhancement.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Service name only | `div` | `govuk-service-navigation` | A service needs a clear name but no persistent navigation. |
| Service name and navigation | `nav` | `govuk-service-navigation__wrapper` | A service has a small set of persistent top-level destinations. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise govuk-service-navigation to reveal and operate the responsive menu toggle.
- Without JavaScript, navigation links remain visible and usable and the toggle remains hidden.
- Mark the current destination with the official current-item option and accessible current-page semantics.

#### Accessibility contract

- Give the nav a concise aria-label that distinguishes it from other navigation landmarks.
- Give the toggle an aria-controls value matching the navigation list id.
- Do not communicate the current page through styling alone.

#### Content rules

- Use the public service name consistently with the page title and service start page.
- Use concise nouns for destinations and avoid duplicating links already provided by the browser or page content.
- Do not include GOV.UK global navigation items in this service-level component.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.brand`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`

#### HTML examples

##### Service navigation links

```html
<section class="govuk-service-navigation" aria-label="Service information" data-module="govuk-service-navigation">
  <div class="govuk-width-container"><div class="govuk-service-navigation__container">
    <span class="govuk-service-navigation__service-name"><a class="govuk-service-navigation__link" href="/">Example service</a></span>
    <nav aria-label="Menu" class="govuk-service-navigation__wrapper">
      <button type="button" class="govuk-service-navigation__toggle govuk-js-service-navigation-toggle" aria-controls="service-navigation" hidden aria-hidden="true">Menu</button>
      <ul class="govuk-service-navigation__list" id="service-navigation"><li class="govuk-service-navigation__item govuk-service-navigation__item--active"><a class="govuk-service-navigation__link" href="/account" aria-current="true"><strong class="govuk-service-navigation__active-fallback">Your account</strong></a></li></ul>
    </nav>
  </div></div>
</section>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/service-navigation/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/service-navigation)

### Skip link

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a skip link as the first focusable control so keyboard users can bypass repeated navigation and move to main content.

#### When to use

- Include on every page with repeated header or navigation content.
- Target the unique main-content landmark ID.

#### When not to use

- Do not omit it because the page appears short at one viewport size.
- Do not point it at an element that is missing, hidden or earlier in the focus order.

#### Anatomy

- **Skip anchor (required):** A govuk-skip-link with a fragment href appears at the start of body content.
- **Target landmark (required):** The fragment resolves to the main element's unique ID.
- **Module hook (required):** data-module=govuk-skip-link enables supported target-focus handling.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `a` | `govuk-skip-link` | The first focusable element in the GOV.UK page template. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise GOV.UK Frontend so the module can manage focus on targets that are not naturally focusable.
- The anchor and fragment still provide useful navigation without JavaScript.
- Do not intercept activation or replace fragment navigation with scrolling alone.

#### Accessibility contract

- Keep the link first in the useful keyboard order and visibly expose it on focus.
- Use a stable target such as main#main-content and verify focus moves there in supported browsers.
- Localise the link text for the page language.

#### Content rules

- Use “Skip to main content” unless the target has a clearer established localised label.
- Do not add several skip links unless the page structure and user testing demonstrate a need.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.link`

#### HTML examples

##### Main-content skip link

```html
<a href="#main-content" class="govuk-skip-link" data-module="govuk-skip-link">Skip to main content</a>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/skip-link/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/skip-link)

### Summary list

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a summary list to present related key-and-value facts, optionally with contextual actions or a summary-card heading.

#### When to use

- Use for facts that each have a clear key and at least one value.
- Use summary cards for several records of the same type, such as people or appointments.
- Add actions when users can change or remove the corresponding information.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for tabular comparisons; use a Table.
- Do not use for an ordinary sequence or task list.
- Do not force content without a meaningful key-value relationship into a description list.

#### Anatomy

- **Description list (required):** A govuk-summary-list dl contains repeated row wrappers.
- **Key and value (required):** Each row contains a dt key and dd value.
- **Actions:** An optional dd contains links with visually hidden row context.
- **Card heading:** A summary card can group a list with a heading and whole-card actions.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Summary list | `dl` | `govuk-summary-list` | One group of key-value facts. |
| Without borders | `dl` | `govuk-summary-list`, `govuk-summary-list--no-border` | A short simple list where row borders add unnecessary visual weight. |
| Summary card | `div` | `govuk-summary-card` | One of several comparable records requiring its own heading or actions. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required and action links use ordinary href navigation.
- Keep rows in a meaningful order and retain the semantic dl, dt and dd elements.
- After a change action, return users to the correct review context where possible.

#### Accessibility contract

- Add visually hidden key context to repeated action labels, for example “Change name”.
- Set the card heading level to fit the page hierarchy.
- Do not create empty keys or values merely to preserve a visual grid.

#### Content rules

- Keep keys concise and use the same terms as the questions that collected the data.
- Format values for reading rather than exposing raw storage values.
- Use consistent action verbs such as “Change” and “Remove”.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`

#### HTML examples

##### Facts with contextual action

```html
<dl class="govuk-summary-list">
  <div class="govuk-summary-list__row">
    <dt class="govuk-summary-list__key">Name</dt>
    <dd class="govuk-summary-list__value">Alex Smith</dd>
    <dd class="govuk-summary-list__actions"><a class="govuk-link" href="/name">Change<span class="govuk-visually-hidden"> name</span></a></dd>
  </div>
</dl>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/summary-list/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/summary-list)

### Table

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a table to let users compare structured data across rows and columns.

#### When to use

- Use when information has consistent row and column relationships that users need to compare.
- Use numeric column classes for numbers that benefit from right alignment and tabular figures.

#### When not to use

- Do not use a table for page layout.
- Do not use for a simple key-value record; use a Summary list.
- Do not put unrelated content into columns only to save vertical space.

#### Anatomy

- **Table and caption (required):** A govuk-table has a descriptive caption, which may be visually hidden if an equivalent heading is already present.
- **Column headings (required):** A thead uses th scope=col for each column label.
- **Body rows (required):** Rows contain th scope=row where the first cell identifies the row, followed by data cells.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `table` | `govuk-table` | Textual row-and-column data. |
| Numeric columns | `th` | `govuk-table__header`, `govuk-table__header--numeric` | Values such as prices, counts and measurements that should align by digit. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The table has no GOV.UK JavaScript behaviour.
- For narrow screens, simplify columns or provide an intentional responsive treatment without changing relationships.
- If sorting is added, use a separately tested accessible pattern; base GOV.UK Table is not sortable.

#### Accessibility contract

- Provide a caption and use scope attributes so headers are associated with their data.
- Keep a logical source order and do not rely on colour or position alone for meaning.
- Avoid horizontal scrolling for ordinary data; when unavoidable, keep keyboard access and visible context.

#### Content rules

- Use concise column headings with consistent units and formatting.
- Align comparable numeric values and include currency or measurement units clearly.
- Do not leave ambiguous empty cells; use meaningful text when absence itself matters.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`
- `govuk.typography.scale.19.mobile-font-size`

#### HTML examples

##### Monthly costs

```html
<table class="govuk-table">
  <caption class="govuk-table__caption govuk-table__caption--m">Monthly costs</caption>
  <thead class="govuk-table__head"><tr class="govuk-table__row"><th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header">Month</th><th scope="col" class="govuk-table__header govuk-table__header--numeric">Amount</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody class="govuk-table__body"><tr class="govuk-table__row"><th scope="row" class="govuk-table__header">January</th><td class="govuk-table__cell govuk-table__cell--numeric">£85</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/table/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/table)

### Tabs

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Tabs to let experienced users switch between closely related sections of content without leaving the page.

#### When to use

- Use for users who are familiar with tabbed interfaces, such as caseworkers switching between related data views.
- Use only when users do not need to compare the sections at the same time.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for primary page or site navigation, or to hide steps in a journey.
- Do not use when users need to read sections in order or compare information across them.

#### Anatomy

- **Tabs module (required):** The root contains a fallback contents heading, link list and corresponding panels.
- **Tab links (required):** Each ordinary anchor targets the id of one content panel.
- **Panels (required):** Each uniquely identified panel contains a heading and its complete content.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-tabs` | Two or more closely related content views for experienced users. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise govuk-tabs so wide screens receive tab semantics, keyboard behaviour and history-fragment updates.
- On narrow screens and without JavaScript, links and panels behave as an in-page table of contents rather than an inaccessible tab widget.
- Do not manually add ARIA tab roles; allow the official GOV.UK module to enhance the base markup.

#### Accessibility contract

- Every tab href must match one unique panel id and every panel needs a descriptive heading.
- Keep all content in the document so it remains reachable before enhancement.
- Test keyboard navigation, back and forward navigation, and layouts at high zoom.

#### Content rules

- Use short, distinct tab labels that describe the panel content.
- Keep the number of tabs small enough to remain understandable and usable on narrow screens.
- Do not repeat the same information in multiple panels.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.body-background`

#### HTML examples

##### Two related views

```html
<div class="govuk-tabs" data-module="govuk-tabs">
  <h2 class="govuk-tabs__title">Contents</h2>
  <ul class="govuk-tabs__list">
    <li class="govuk-tabs__list-item govuk-tabs__list-item--selected"><a class="govuk-tabs__tab" href="#today">Today</a></li>
    <li class="govuk-tabs__list-item"><a class="govuk-tabs__tab" href="#this-week">This week</a></li>
  </ul>
  <div class="govuk-tabs__panel" id="today"><h2 class="govuk-heading-l">Today</h2><p class="govuk-body">Today’s information.</p></div>
  <div class="govuk-tabs__panel govuk-tabs__panel--hidden" id="this-week"><h2 class="govuk-heading-l">This week</h2><p class="govuk-body">This week’s information.</p></div>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/tabs/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/tabs)

### Tag

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a tag to show a concise status or category that helps users scan related information.

#### When to use

- Use to label an item's current status in a list, table, task list or banner.
- Use a documented colour variant only when a consistent status meaning exists across the service.

#### When not to use

- Do not use tags as buttons, links or interactive filters.
- Do not use a tag merely to decorate or emphasise ordinary text.
- Do not create many colour meanings that users must memorise.

#### Anatomy

- **Tag element (required):** A govuk-tag wraps a short status label; choose an element that fits the surrounding semantics.
- **Status label (required):** Brief text communicates the status without relying on the background colour.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default blue | `strong` | `govuk-tag` | A status where no documented semantic colour variant is needed. |
| Green | `strong` | `govuk-tag`, `govuk-tag--green` | A positive or completed state, used consistently. |
| Red | `strong` | `govuk-tag`, `govuk-tag--red` | A stopped, rejected or urgent negative state, used consistently. |
| Grey | `strong` | `govuk-tag`, `govuk-tag--grey` | An inactive, closed or neutral state. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Tags have no JavaScript behaviour and must not receive interactive roles or click handlers.
- Keep status terminology and colour mapping consistent across the product.

#### Accessibility contract

- The label text must communicate the full status independently of colour.
- Make repeated tags meaningful in their row or item context.
- Do not add tabindex to a non-interactive tag.

#### Content rules

- Use one to three short words and sentence case unless the product's established status vocabulary requires otherwise.
- Prefer specific labels such as “Completed” or “Needs review” over vague labels such as “Status 2”.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.brand`
- `govuk.color.success`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`

#### HTML examples

##### Completed status

```html
<strong class="govuk-tag govuk-tag--green">Completed</strong>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/tag/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/tag)

### Task list

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a task list to show the tasks in a multi-part service and help users understand which are complete or still need attention.

#### When to use

- Use for services with several tasks that users may complete over time or in a flexible order.
- Show a clear current status for each task and link only tasks the user can open.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for a short linear journey where normal page navigation is clearer.
- Do not use as a generic navigation menu or checklist unrelated to completing a service.

#### Anatomy

- **Task list (required):** A govuk-task-list ul contains one li per task.
- **Task name and hint (required):** The task has a concise name, optional hint and an href only when it is available.
- **Status (required):** A uniquely identified status is referenced from the task link using aria-describedby.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linked task | `li` | `govuk-task-list__item`, `govuk-task-list__item--with-link` | A task the user can currently open. |
| Unlinked task | `li` | `govuk-task-list__item` | A task that is unavailable or does not have a destination. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required; links navigate to the corresponding task.
- Derive status from authoritative service data and update it after task completion.
- Do not make the status itself the only clickable target when the task name is the destination.

#### Accessibility contract

- Associate each link with its unique status ID using aria-describedby.
- Status text must be meaningful without its tag colour.
- Keep list order and task availability understandable to keyboard and screen-reader users.

#### Content rules

- Name each task with a concise verb phrase or recognisable subject.
- Use a small consistent status vocabulary, such as “Not started”, “In progress” and “Completed”.
- Add hint text only when the task name does not provide enough context.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`

#### HTML examples

##### One task with status

```html
<ul class="govuk-task-list">
  <li class="govuk-task-list__item govuk-task-list__item--with-link">
    <div class="govuk-task-list__name-and-hint"><a class="govuk-link govuk-task-list__link" href="/company-details" aria-describedby="company-details-status">Company details</a></div>
    <div class="govuk-task-list__status" id="company-details-status">Completed</div>
  </li>
</ul>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/task-list/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/task-list)

### Text input

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a text input when a user needs to enter a short amount of text that cannot be selected from predetermined options.

#### When to use

- Use for a short free-text answer such as a name, reference, or account identifier.
- Choose a width that communicates the expected answer length when the expected format is known.
- Add hint text only when it helps users provide the requested information.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for long answers; use the textarea component.
- Do not use free text when users should select from a small, known set of options.
- Do not set a maximum length merely to force visual width; input width and data validation are separate concerns.

#### Anatomy

- **Form group (required):** Groups the label, optional hint, optional error, and input. Error state adds govuk-form-group--error.
- **Label (required):** A visible label is programmatically associated to the input using for and id.
- **Hint:** Supplementary guidance is referenced from aria-describedby when present.
- **Error message:** An error is visible, includes a visually hidden Error prefix, and is referenced from aria-describedby.
- **Input (required):** The native input keeps a stable id and name and receives the govuk-input class.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `input` | `govuk-input` | A short free-text answer whose expected length is not usefully constrained visually. |
| Fixed width | `input` | `govuk-input`, `govuk-input--width-10` | An answer with a predictable maximum presentation length, such as a National Insurance number. |
| Error | `input` | `govuk-input`, `govuk-input--error` | Redisplay an invalid answer with a specific error message and linked error summary. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The text input itself requires no GOV.UK JavaScript.
- On validation failure, retain the user's answer unless doing so would expose sensitive information.
- Server-side validation remains authoritative even when client-side validation is also used.

#### Accessibility contract

- Every input must have a visible label associated using matching for and id values.
- List hint IDs before error IDs in aria-describedby so supporting information is announced in a useful order.
- Add govuk-input--error and govuk-form-group--error together; colour alone is not the error message.
- Use an appropriate autocomplete token and input mode when the requested data has a defined purpose or keyboard layout.

#### Content rules

- Ask one clear question and use the label as the primary prompt.
- Do not use placeholder text as a substitute for a label or persistent hint.
- Error messages should explain what went wrong and how to correct it without blaming the user.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.text`

#### HTML examples

##### Input with hint and error

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group govuk-form-group--error">
  <label class="govuk-label" for="national-insurance-number">
    National Insurance number
  </label>
  <div id="national-insurance-number-hint" class="govuk-hint">
    It is on your National Insurance card, benefit letter, payslip or P60.
  </div>
  <p id="national-insurance-number-error" class="govuk-error-message">
    <span class="govuk-visually-hidden">Error:</span> Enter a National Insurance number in the correct format
  </p>
  <input class="govuk-input govuk-input--width-10 govuk-input--error" id="national-insurance-number" name="nationalInsuranceNumber" type="text" spellcheck="false" aria-describedby="national-insurance-number-hint national-insurance-number-error">
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/text-input/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/input)

### Textarea

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use a textarea when users need to enter more than one line of free text.

#### When to use

- Use when the expected answer may contain sentences or several lines.
- Set rows to suggest a useful starting height without restricting how much users can enter.

#### When not to use

- Use a Text input for a short single-line answer.
- Use Character count when a genuine, user-understood maximum length must be enforced.
- Do not ask for large free-text answers when structured questions would be easier to answer and process.

#### Anatomy

- **Form group (required):** Groups the visible label, optional hint, optional error and textarea.
- **Label (required):** A visible label is associated using for and id.
- **Native textarea (required):** The govuk-textarea supports multi-line input and browser resizing.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `textarea` | `govuk-textarea` | A multi-line answer without a strict character limit. |
| Error | `textarea` | `govuk-textarea`, `govuk-textarea--error` | Redisplay an invalid answer with a linked error message. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- The base textarea requires no GOV.UK JavaScript.
- Allow native resizing and retain the submitted answer after recoverable validation errors.
- Validate on the server and store line breaks safely.

#### Accessibility contract

- Associate a visible label and reference hint and error IDs in aria-describedby.
- Do not use placeholder text instead of a label or hint.
- Do not disable browser resizing or clip enlarged text.

#### Content rules

- Ask a focused question and explain what information to include.
- Say how the answer will be used when users may disclose sensitive information.
- Avoid unnecessary maximum lengths; when one is necessary explain it before input.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.input-border`
- `govuk.color.error`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`

#### HTML examples

##### More detail

```html
<div class="govuk-form-group">
  <label class="govuk-label" for="more-detail">Can you provide more detail?</label>
  <textarea class="govuk-textarea" id="more-detail" name="moreDetail" rows="5"></textarea>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/textarea/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/textarea)

### Warning text

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use warning text to alert users to an important consequence of an action or inaction.

#### When to use

- Use when users need to understand a serious consequence before deciding what to do.
- Place it immediately before the related action or decision when timing matters.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for ordinary guidance, validation errors or successful outcomes.
- Do not show several warning-text components on one page, which makes it difficult to identify the most important consequence.

#### Anatomy

- **Warning container (required):** A govuk-warning-text groups the icon and message.
- **Decorative icon (required):** The exclamation mark is hidden from assistive technology using aria-hidden.
- **Warning message (required):** Strong text contains a visually hidden Warning label followed by the consequence.

#### Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-warning-text` | A serious consequence on the standard page background. |

#### Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required.
- Keep the warning adjacent to the action or information it qualifies.

#### Accessibility contract

- Retain aria-hidden on the icon and the govuk-visually-hidden Warning text.
- The consequence must be understandable without seeing the icon, weight or layout.
- Do not use warning styling as the only indication that an action has risk.

#### Content rules

- State the specific consequence in plain language.
- Avoid vague phrases such as “Warning: be careful” and do not duplicate “Warning” in visible text.
- Tell users what they can do to avoid the consequence when that is not obvious.

#### Token references

- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`
- `govuk.typography.weight.bold`
- `govuk.border.standard`

#### HTML examples

##### Registration warning

```html
<div class="govuk-warning-text">
  <span class="govuk-warning-text__icon" aria-hidden="true">!</span>
  <strong class="govuk-warning-text__text">
    <span class="govuk-visually-hidden">Warning</span>
    You can be fined up to £5,000 if you do not register.
  </strong>
</div>
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/warning-text/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/components/warning-text)

## 6. Motion & Interaction

Use the component-specific behaviour and progressive-enhancement contracts above. Preserve visible keyboard focus and native control semantics. Essential content and service actions must remain available without JavaScript; initialise GOV.UK Frontend modules for supported enhancements.

## 7. Iconography & Imagery

### Images

**Foundation group:** visual elements  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use images only for a demonstrated user need and ensure their information remains available to people who cannot see them.

#### Rules

- Begin with clear written content and add an image only when research shows that it helps users understand or complete the service.
- Treat an image as a visual aid; all information needed to complete the task must also exist in text or another accessible form.
- Use photography, illustration and icons consistently and avoid decorative stock imagery.
- Avoid images containing text because the text cannot reflow, translate or respond reliably to user settings.
- Supply intrinsic width and height and responsive sizing to reduce layout shifts without cropping essential information.

#### Accessibility contract

- Write concise alt text that communicates the image's purpose in context; use an empty alt attribute for a genuinely decorative image.
- Do not repeat nearby visible text in alt text or begin it with image of.
- For complex diagrams, provide the equivalent information in adjacent text or a linked accessible description.
- Maintain sufficient contrast for meaningful details and do not communicate distinctions by colour alone.

#### Restrictions and caveats

- Do not copy or redistribute GOV.UK crowns, logotypes, favicons or other identity assets from this repository; obtain approved assets through official GOV.UK Frontend channels when the service is eligible.
- Do not replace a native control or a text label with an unexplained icon.

#### Token references

No portable token is appropriate for this guidance.

#### Examples

##### Informative responsive image

```html
<img src="/assets/permit-example.webp" alt="Permit number highlighted in the top-right corner" width="800" height="450" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto">
```

#### Authoritative sources

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/styles/images/)
- [GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 implementation](https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend/tree/v6.5.0/packages/govuk-frontend/src/govuk/assets)

Use the documented component markup for icons. GOV.UK identity assets and GDS Transport have eligibility requirements and are not embedded in this file.

## 8. Voice & Tone

Follow the content rules in each component and the journey rules below. Use clear sentence-case action labels that describe the outcome, meaningful labels and specific error messages. Preserve the distinction between links for navigation and buttons for actions.

## 9. Edge Cases & Variations

Apply the following patterns to the full service journey, including validation, errors, confirmation and accessibility. Treat accessibility as a service-level responsibility and test the implemented service with users and assistive technology.

### Addresses

**Pattern group:** ask users for  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Help users provide an address using separate fields, an address lookup with a manual fallback, or a textarea chosen for the service’s data needs.

#### When to use

- Use whenever an address is genuinely required to deliver the service.
- Choose the input approach according to the countries covered and whether the service needs structured address parts.

#### When not to use

- Do not force international addresses into a UK-only structure or lookup.
- Do not collect county or other address parts unless the service uses them.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Use separate fields when supported countries share a workable structure; keep address line 2 and county optional unless there is a proven need.
- For a UK address lookup, accept flexible postcode formatting and always provide a clear manual-entry route.
- Use a textarea with autocomplete=street-address only when free-form addresses are usable and structured parts are unnecessary.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Apply the correct autocomplete purpose to each address field and associate every hint and error with its input.
- Make lookup results and the manual alternative keyboard and screen-reader accessible, including when JavaScript fails.

- [error-message](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-message/)

### Bank details

**Pattern group:** ask users for  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Ask for bank or building-society account details in familiar separate fields, accepting the formats people normally use.

#### When to use

- Use when the service must pay money into or collect money from a UK bank or building-society account.
- Collect only the fields needed for the transaction and applicable validation.

#### When not to use

- Do not ask for bank details before the user understands why they are needed and how they will be protected.
- Do not confuse bank details with payment-card details.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Use separate fields for name on the account, sort code, account number and an optional building-society roll number.
- Use text inputs with numeric input mode where helpful; do not use number inputs because leading zeroes and spacing matter.
- Accept common separators and normalise input safely rather than demanding one visual format.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Keep every label visible and associate format hints and specific errors using aria-describedby.
- Do not prevent pasting, password-manager assistance or assistive input methods.

- [text-input](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/text-input/)

#### Related patterns

### Check a service is suitable

**Pattern group:** help users to  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Ask a short sequence of simple questions so users can learn early whether a service is suitable, what it costs or what outcome they may receive.

#### When to use

- Use when eligibility, cost, timescale or likely outcome is too complicated to explain clearly on the start page.
- Help users find out whether the service meets their need before collecting application details.

#### When not to use

- Do not build a checker when concise start-page content can explain the criteria.
- Do not disguise policy decisions or deny users a route to understand and challenge an outcome.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Begin with an introduction, ask one simple question per page and calculate the relevant result from the answers.
- End every branch with a clear results page that explains suitability and what the user can do next.
- Put fixed rules such as universal age limits or deadlines on the start page as well as in the checker.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Use semantic question pages with visible legends or labels and preserve answers when users go back.
- Write result pages in plain language and provide an accessible alternative when the automated decision cannot cover a user’s situation.

#### Related components

- [radios](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)
- [checkboxes](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/checkboxes/)
- [button](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/button/)
- [back-link](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/back-link/)

#### Related patterns

- [question-pages](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/question-pages/)
- [start-using-a-service](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/start-using-a-service/)

#### Authoritative source

- [Usage guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/check-a-service-is-suitable/)

### Check answers

**Pattern group:** help users to  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Let users review and change the information they provided before they submit a transaction.

#### When to use

- Use before a final submission when users need to confirm that collected information is correct.
- Group answers into meaningful sections that match the journey.

#### When not to use

- Do not add a check page to a very short, low-risk interaction unless research shows it helps.
- Do not make users restart the journey to correct one answer.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Use Summary list rows for question-and-answer pairs and add a specific change link for every editable answer.
- Change links must return users to the check page after editing and retain other answers.
- Make the final action explicit and explain any declaration, legal effect or next step before the button.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Append visually hidden context to repeated change links so each has a unique accessible name.
- Render answers as text rather than disabled form controls and preserve a logical heading hierarchy.

- [summary-list](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/summary-list/)
- [button](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/button/)

#### Related patterns

### Complete multiple tasks

**Pattern group:** help users to  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Use a task-list journey to show which tasks are required, their helpful order and each task’s current status.

#### When to use

- Use for transactions with several tasks that users may complete over more than one session or in a flexible order.
- Use statuses when users need to understand what is complete, incomplete or not yet available.

#### When not to use

- Do not use for a short linear service where a series of question pages is clearer.
- Do not use the GOV.UK content-site Step by step navigation pattern inside a transaction.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Group tasks under meaningful headings and order them according to dependencies and user needs.
- Use links only for tasks the user can currently act on and show accurate, consistently worded status text.
- Return to the task list after completing a task and derive status from saved service data rather than presentation state.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Connect every task link to its status with the component’s described-by relationship.
- Do not rely on tag colour to communicate status and ensure non-link tasks explain why they are unavailable.

### Confirm a phone number

**Pattern group:** help users to  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Check that a user currently has access to a mobile number by sending a time-limited security code in a text message.

#### When to use

- Use when access to a particular mobile number is necessary for a proportionate service or account security need.
- Provide a resend and correction route for delayed messages or an incorrect number.

#### When not to use

- Do not treat control of a phone number as proof of a person’s identity.
- Do not make text-message confirmation the only route when users may not have mobile access or reliable signal.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Send a short single-use code, set an expiry and limit attempts and resend abuse without locking legitimate users out indefinitely.
- Use a type=text field with inputmode=numeric, autocomplete=one-time-code and enough width and letter spacing for the code.
- Explain the destination number safely, when the code expires, how to resend it and how to change the number.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Do not split the code into one input per character; one labelled field supports paste and assistive input more reliably.
- Announce resend outcomes and errors clearly without starting an inaccessible visual-only countdown.

- [text-input](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/text-input/)

- [notification-banner](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/notification-banner/)

### Confirm an email address

**Pattern group:** help users to  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Check that a user currently has access to an email account using a carefully designed confirmation link or code loop.

#### When to use

- Use only when critical functionality depends on email or a mistyped address could expose sensitive information to someone else.
- Choose a blocking or non-blocking loop according to the risk and the user’s need to continue.

#### When not to use

- Do not confirm email by default for low-impact messages or receipts.
- Do not treat a confirmed address as proof of identity; it only proves access at the time of confirmation.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Make confirmation links single-use and time-limited, and expire them when superseded or when the account email changes.
- Let users resend the message and change a mistyped address without losing journey data.
- Explain that the user must switch to email and return, and design the activation landing page for both same-device and cross-device use.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Write a clear email subject and link purpose, and do not rely on a long raw URL as the only activation route.
- Provide support or an alternative path for users who cannot access email and make status messages available to assistive technology.

#### Related components

- [text-input](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/text-input/)
- [button](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/button/)
- [notification-banner](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/notification-banner/)

- [create-accounts](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/create-accounts/)

### Confirmation pages

**Pattern group:** pages  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Tell users that they have completed a transaction, give them any reference and explain what will happen next.

#### When to use

- Use immediately after a user successfully completes a transaction.
- Give a reference when users or support staff will need it later.

#### When not to use

- Do not use a success page before the service has durably accepted the transaction.
- Do not rely on email or another later message as the only confirmation.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Use a Confirmation panel with a clear completed-action heading and the reference number when applicable.
- Below the panel, explain what happens next, expected timescales, any action the user must take and how confirmation will be delivered.
- Prevent accidental duplicate submissions on refresh and provide a relevant feedback link.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Make the success heading the page H1 and present the reference as selectable text rather than only in an image.
- Do not communicate success through the green panel colour alone; the text must state the outcome.

#### Related components

- [panel](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/panel/)

### Contact a department or service team

**Pattern group:** help users to  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Give users complete, contextual contact information at the point they are likely to need help.

#### When to use

- Use wherever research shows users need to contact the responsible team during or after a service journey.
- Offer the contact channels the team can reliably support.

#### When not to use

- Do not hide essential contact routes behind vague help links or a channel users may not be able to access.
- Do not publish contact details without ownership, opening-hours and maintenance arrangements.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- For phone support, include the number, opening times, closures, any textphone or Welsh-language route and a call-charges link where relevant.
- For email or webchat, state expected response or availability and what information users should prepare.
- Use a specific heading such as “Get help with your application” and keep the information close to the task context.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Provide more than one usable channel where possible and explain relay, textphone or other accessibility support.
- Use readable text and descriptive links rather than presenting contact details only in images, scripts or icons.

### Cookies page

**Pattern group:** pages  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Explain every cookie the service sets and let users review and change consent for categories of non-essential cookies.

#### When to use

- Provide a cookies page whenever the service stores cookies or similar data on a user’s device.
- Let users change optional-cookie preferences after responding to the Cookie banner.

#### When not to use

- Do not present strictly necessary cookies as optional or set non-essential cookies before a valid consent choice.
- Do not use generic copied cookie lists that differ from what the deployed service actually sets.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Explain what cookies are, why the service uses each category and that essential cookies do not require consent.
- For each cookie list its name, purpose and expiry, and keep the page synchronised with production behaviour and third parties.
- Provide equivalent accept and reject controls for optional categories, store the choice and confirm when it changes.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Use properly captioned tables with scoped headers and real form controls with a fieldset and legend for each choice group.
- Make saving preferences work without JavaScript and expose the outcome in a clear notification.

### Create a username

**Pattern group:** help users to  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Help users create or use a memorable unique username only after establishing that the service needs accounts.

#### When to use

- Prefer an email address as the username when users have one and the service already needs it.
- Use a custom username only where user-generated content needs a public attribution that can protect the person’s identity.

#### When not to use

- Do not ask users to invent a username merely because an account system supports one.
- Do not exclude users without email; research and provide a supported alternative.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Check uniqueness, suggest an available alternative when useful and ignore letter case during sign-in.
- Let users retrieve or reset a forgotten username and change their email address or username later.
- Explain any permitted characters before entry and avoid arbitrary rules that make a username difficult to remember.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Use one visible labelled text field and announce availability results without relying on colour or client-side JavaScript.
- Keep suggestions understandable and editable instead of silently assigning an identifier.

### Create accounts

**Pattern group:** help users to  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Create an account only when users need recurring access to their service data, and defer account creation until it becomes necessary.

#### When to use

- Use when users need to regularly access, manage or update information held by the service.
- Let users complete as much of the journey as possible before requiring the account.

#### When not to use

- Do not create accounts when a usable one-off service can work without them.
- Do not use an account merely to let users check one transaction when a safely delivered reference can meet the need.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Call the action “Create an account” and clearly separate account creation from sign-in.
- Use action labels such as “Create a username” and “Create a password” so users know they are setting new credentials.
- Design recovery, email or phone changes, account closure, data retention and fraud controls as part of the journey.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Do not make account recovery depend on one inaccessible channel and allow password managers and paste.
- Preserve entered journey data if account creation interrupts an in-progress service.

### Dates

**Pattern group:** ask users for  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Help users provide or select a date using an interaction suited to whether the date is memorable, copied from a document, approximate or selected from known options.

#### When to use

- Use whenever a service asks users to provide or select a date.
- Use Date input for memorable dates such as a date of birth or a date copied from a document.

#### When not to use

- Do not use a calendar picker for dates users know or can copy more easily by typing.
- Do not require day-level precision when the service only needs a month, year or approximate date.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- State the expected precision and show a relevant example without pre-filling an answer.
- Store and validate the date as separate semantic values or a safe date type, not by assuming the display string is unambiguous.
- Use radios or another simple selection control when users choose from a small known set of dates.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Group day, month and year controls with a fieldset, legend and a shared hint.
- Report which part of a date is invalid and preserve all values when re-rendering errors.

### Email addresses

**Pattern group:** ask users for  
**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09

Ask for an email address in one field, explain why it is needed and accept the broad range of valid addresses users may have.

#### When to use

- Use whenever the service genuinely needs to capture an email address.
- Explain the purpose, especially when it will be used for receipts, updates or account recovery.

#### When not to use

- Do not assume every user has reliable access to email when another channel can meet the need.
- Do not add a confirmation loop unless the separate Confirm an email address pattern’s high-impact conditions apply.

#### Journey and implementation rules

- Use a single type=email text input with autocomplete=email and spellcheck disabled.
- Accept valid address characters and avoid validation rules that reject uncommon but valid domains or formats.
- Let users paste and correct the address; do not ask them to type it twice.

#### Accessibility and service safeguards

- Use a visible label and connect the purpose hint and any specific error to the input.
- Do not rely on browser-native validation messages; use the service’s accessible validation flow.
